# pantoken

Instructure design tokens and icons, reshaped for every platform. pantoken resolves Instructure UI's
tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then emits many small, individually-publishable
packages — CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus, React/Vue/Svelte, Tailwind/Panda, native Swift/Kotlin, WordPress,
Figma, and more — unified by an unscoped `pantoken` meta package.

Read `README.md` for the consumer quickstart. This file is the map to everything an agent needs; open
the linked docs only when a task calls for them.

## How to work here

- **Use the `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` CLIs — never raw pnpm, npm, or yarn.** They're global bins. Package
  scripts must never shell out to `pnpm` internally: CI provides `vp` but not `pnpm` on PATH, so a
  `pnpm run …` inside a script breaks the docs deploy. Details in `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start.** "Port in use" is not "stale" — the user runs their own
  dev servers in other windows. For your own preview server, bind a distinct port with `--strictPort`.
  If a port is taken, pick another or ask.
- **Decide one fork at a time.** Give a recommendation plus the tradeoff, then let the user choose.
  Verify third-party claims (upstream token names, browser support, a library's capability) before
  asserting them.
- **Writing:** active voice, contractions, plain language, Oxford comma. Don't use empowering,
  harnessing, unlocking, supercharging, transforming, game-changing, seamless, robust, leverage, or
  synergy.
- **Keep `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/web-components` runtime graphs Node-free** — they ship
  to the browser. A value import of a postcss-based `@cssdoc/*` package pulls a `node:module` shim
  into the bundle and kills client JS. Type-only imports are fine; value imports belong in build
  scripts and tests.
- **Generate a changeset for every user-visible change.** Run `pnpm changeset` and commit the
  `.changeset/*.md` file alongside the code change.
- **When refining user-facing packages, evaluate `@pantoken/ai` in the same change.** If package
  recommendations, CLI target examples, or usage conventions changed, update the consumer agent assets
  in `ai/pantoken-ai` so assistant guidance does not drift.
- **Keep security docs current.** When a code change alters a threat, adds a control, or closes a
  residual risk in `ASSURANCE.md`, update both `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` before merging.

## Knowledge map

| When you need to…                                                                  | Read…                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Understand the monorepo, the pipeline, and why `@pantoken/model` exists            | `docs/architecture/overview.md`      |
| Author or extend a component (records, the modifier convention, aliases, `@scope`) | `docs/conventions/authoring.md`      |
| Work on the web components (shadow CSS, `register()`/prefix, the JS-behavior tier) | `docs/conventions/web-components.md` |
| Run more than one theme or color scheme in a single document                       | `docs/conventions/scoping.md`        |
| Build, lint, release, or work on the docs site + i18n + cssdoc integration         | `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` |
| Avoid re-solving a known bug or gotcha                                             | `docs/engineering-log.md`            |
| Amend the security assurance case after adding a new input surface or control      | `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`        |
| Match an agent to a domain                                                         | `AGENTS.md`                          |

## Repo shape

Organized by _how you consume_ each package: `packages/` core machinery · `formats/` importable
serializations (css, icons, scss, components, …) · `platforms/` generated foreign-ecosystem source ·
`renderers/` UI integrations (web-components, framework wrappers, bridges) · `bundlers/` build-pipeline
plugins · `design/` Figma + swatches · `plugins/{pantoken,postcss,typedoc,vite}/` · `tools/` internal
build tooling · `ai/` consumer-facing agent assets. The gate is `pnpm run ready` +
`pnpm run check:publish`.

# `@pantoken/web-components`

Shadow-DOM custom elements built over the `@pantoken/components` CSS. A `wrapper(tag, css, render,
display)` covers pure-presentational elements; behavioral elements are bespoke classes.

## Runtime graph must stay Node-free

This package ships to the browser (the docs client registers it). Anything in the runtime graph is
bundled into the client. A **value** import of a postcss-based `@cssdoc/*` package makes rolldown
inject a `createRequire`/`node:module` shim into `dist/index.mjs`, which throws `createRequire is not
a function` at app init and kills all client JS. Keep `@cssdoc/*` value imports out of `src/` —
type-only imports are fine (erased at build); value imports belong in build scripts and tests.

## Shadow CSS is co-located `.css` → `?inline`

- Shadow CSS lives in co-located `src/**/*.css` files — the lint, format, and docs source of truth.
- Elements import their co-located CSS with `?inline`; Vite+ bundles `@tsdown/css`, which returns the
  processed stylesheet as a tree-shakeable string for the shadow `<style>`.
- The CSS finalizer strips doc comments and minifies the inline string, so cssdoc records stay in the
  source `.css` files without shipping as runtime bytes.
- Use `?inline`, not `?raw`: `?inline` is the shared Vite/`@tsdown/css` contract and works in pack,
  dev, and test.

## `register()` and the tag prefix

`register(target?, { prefix })`. The `prefix` option is typed `string` — `null` is a type error, unlike
`@pantoken/components`, where `prefix: null` opts out. A prefix is **always** applied because a custom-element name must
contain a hyphen (`<icon>` is invalid). A non-empty string wins (`{prefix:"x"}` → `<x-icon>`); anything
falsy or whitespace falls back to `DEFAULT_PREFIX = "instui"` — it never drops elements. Implementation
is low-churn: internal code keeps its canonical `instui-<base>` literals, and `register` shadows the
registry with a scoped adapter that rewrites `instui-<base>` → `${prefix}-<base>`. Cross-element
nesting uses `ctx.tag("calendar")` so the prefix propagates.

`register()` also injects `foundationCss()` once into `document.head` as `<style
id="pantoken-foundation">` — a `:root` block built from `elevationDeclarations()` +
`focusOutlineDeclarations()`. Those tokens aren't in the plain token sheet, so without it a consumer
loading only the module + `@pantoken/css` gets no shadows or focus rings (custom props pierce the
shadow boundary). It's guarded on `typeof document` so the registry-only test path skips it, and
exported for SSR inlining.

## Structure

`src/index.ts` is a barrel. Elements are `src/elements/<name>.ts`, one `ElementDefinition` each, added
to `DEFINITIONS[]` and `ELEMENTS[]` in **load-bearing order** (a test asserts `ELEMENTS` matches the
`register()` define order — append new tags at the end). `register()` builds one `RegisterContext`
(`{ registry, tag, I:{prefix:"instui"}, invokerSupported, onCommand, wrapper, variantClass, iconSvg }`)
and hands it to each `def.define(ctx)`.

## The JS-behavior tier

Behavior pure CSS can't cover: tooltip, drilldown, pages, drawer-layout, an interactive calendar, and
date/datetime pickers. The consistent declarative layer is the **Invoker Commands API** — light-DOM
`<button command="…" commandfor="element-id">`:

- `instui-modal`: `--show` / `--close` / `--toggle` (the shadow `<dialog>` can't be a `commandfor`
  target, hence host-level custom commands).
- `instui-drilldown`: `--goto` (reads `data-page`) / `--back`.
- `instui-pages`: `--push` / `--back`.
- `instui-drawer-layout`: `--toggle` / `--open` / `--close`.
- `instui-popover`/`instui-tray`/`instui-context-view`: already native `[popover]`, so the built-in
  `command="toggle-popover"` works with no code.

Drawer-layout keeps InstUI-style regions for its tray and content. Supply nonempty `tray-label`
and `content-label` attributes on the host; they name the corresponding shadow-DOM panes and
update when the attributes change. A label on a slotted heading or navigation element doesn't
name its containing shadow region. Name any additional slotted landmarks separately.

A shared `onCommand(target, handler)` helper adds the `command` listener and, when the API is absent
(`!("command" in HTMLButtonElement.prototype)`), falls back to a click delegate reading the same
attributes. It listens on `target.getRootNode()` so it covers a light-DOM host (document) and the
calendar grid (shadow root). Date helpers use **local** dates (avoid `toISOString` UTC shift).

## Universal spacing

Every element supports `margin`/`padding` (InstUI 1–4-value shorthand) and per-side
`margin-<side>`/`padding-<side>` (physical or logical edges), each value a keyword → token or a raw
CSS length. `lib/helpers.ts` exports `resolveSpace`, `spacingValue`, and `applySpacing(host)`; a
`withSpacing(Ctor)` mixin subclasses each ctor and the scoped registry wraps **every** ctor with it in
`define`, so it's universal with zero per-element code (a per-host MutationObserver re-applies on attr
change).

## Testing

The harness has no DOM lib (happy-dom/jsdom absent), so `tests/index.test.ts` only asserts
registration + pure `iconSvg`. Verify behavior in a real browser. `.focus()` fires no focus events
when `document.hasFocus()` is false (headless) — dispatch a composed `focusin` to exercise focus-show.

# Architecture overview

pantoken resolves Instructure UI's design tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then turns
that single model into many small, individually-publishable packages — plain CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus,
React/Vue/Svelte/Angular, Tailwind/Panda/PostCSS, native Swift/Kotlin/Compose/Flutter, WordPress,
Drupal, Figma, and more. You install the smallest package that fits, or the unified `pantoken` meta
package that re-exports them all.

## The pipeline

`@pantoken/core` (the transformer) resolves the Tokens Studio graph into a canonical,
`@property`-aligned `Token[]` IR — icons rolled in as `<image>` tokens. `@pantoken/tokens` vendors
that IR plus the raw JSON as static files. Every emitter (`css`, `icons`, `astro`, `rehype`,
`swift`, and the rest) consumes the vendored IR. The native path runs `core.toStyleDictionary()`
→ `@pantoken/sd-config` (Style Dictionary v5) → `@pantoken/swift` / `@pantoken/cli`.

## The upstream-decoupling constraint (the load-bearing rule)

`@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` is GitHub-only — no npm publish, no types. `@pantoken/core`
depends on it. So a package that depended on `core` would transitively pull the GitHub-only upstream
into every consumer's install. To prevent that:

- Type contracts live in a zero-dependency **`@pantoken/model`**.
- Web and emitter packages depend on **`model` + `tokens`** (both upstream-free), **never on `core`**.
- `core` carries an ambient `declare module "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens"` shim, since the
  upstream ships no types.

When you add a package, keep it off `core` unless it genuinely runs the transform. Reach for `model`
(types) and `tokens` (the vendored IR) instead.

## Workspace layout — organized by how you consume each package

The axis is consumption, not language. The rule of thumb: **import the output → `formats/`;
generate it into another ecosystem → `platforms/`.**

| Bucket       | What lives here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/`  | Core machinery: `model` (types, zero-dep), `core` (transformer), `utils` (shared resolver + drift helpers), `plugin-kit` (the plugin factory), `cli`, and `pantoken` (the auto-generated meta package).                                                                  |
| `formats/`   | Importable npm serializations of the IR — `tokens`, `css`, `icons`, `dtcg`, `scss`, `less`, `stylus`, `icon-font`, and `components`. You `npm i` and import these.                                                                                                       |
| `platforms/` | Foreign-ecosystem source you _generate_ via the CLI and publish to that ecosystem's registry — `swift`, `android`, `compose`, `flutter`, `wordpress`, `vanilla`, `drupal`, `jekyll`, `hugo`, `email`.                                                                    |
| `renderers/` | Integrations that produce UI — `web-components`, `react`/`vue`/`svelte`/`angular` wrappers, `react-markdown`, `rehype`, `astro`, `pendo`, and CSS-var bridges (`shadcn`, `bootstrap`, `docusaurus`, `vitepress`).                                                        |
| `bundlers/`  | Build-pipeline integrations — `vite`, `tailwind`, `postcss`, `next`, `webpack`, `panda`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `design/`    | Design-tool assets — `figma` (Variables payload) and `swatches` (ASE/GPL/sketchpalette).                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `plugins/`   | Split by kind: `plugins/pantoken/*` are `PantokenPlugin`s (colors, focus/simple-icons/stacking/transition/visual-debug/primitives/logos); `plugins/postcss/*` are PostCSS plugins (prune-custom-props); `plugins/typedoc/*` and `plugins/vite/*` are docs/build tooling. |
| `tools/`     | Internal build tooling — `sd-config` (Style Dictionary, powers the native targets), `aggregate` (builds the meta package).                                                                                                                                               |
| `ai/`        | Consumer-facing agent assets (`@pantoken/ai`, `pantoken-ai`) — NOT for developing pantoken itself. It drops AGENTS.md, llms.txt, and editor rules into a _consumer_ repo.                                                                                                |

## The meta package

`pantoken` is auto-generated by `tools/aggregate`, which scans each package's
`"pantoken": { key, kind }` field. `kind` decides how a package joins the meta:

- `namespace` — eager barrel + subpath.
- `sideEffect` — barrel + an `/inject` subpath.
- `subpath` — subpath only, kept **out** of the eager barrel. Used for heavy React integrations (e.g.
  `react-markdown`, tailwind, panda) so `import "pantoken"` never pulls React or a build config.

`aggregate` only _writes_ the meta. When you remove a package from the meta, delete its orphaned
`packages/pantoken/src/<name>.ts` by hand — aggregate won't.

## Shared helpers

`@pantoken/utils` (deps: `model` + `arkregex`) holds the formerly copy-pasted resolver:
`makeResolver(base, {mode?, overrides?})` (a `var()` + `light-dark()` resolver) and `resolveTokens`,
plus the typed `VAR_RE`/`LIGHT_DARK_RE` regexes, `camelCase`, and `parseHexColor`. It also holds the
drift/validation harness — `unknownReferences(text, ir)` (bridge targets must be real tokens) and
`danglingReferences(css)` (self-containment: every `var()` has a definition in the same output) — plus
the generic token→class engines `colorUtilitiesCss` and `tokenUtilitiesCss`. `utils` must never import
from `components` (it sits below it). `checkPlugins` (the capability guard) lives in `plugin-kit`, not
`utils`.

## The gate

`pnpm run ready` must pass — a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`) that builds once, then fans out `vp check`,
test `-r`, CSS/JS lint, generated-output validation, and markdown lint concurrently. `pnpm run
check:publish` runs the publish gate (repository metadata + publint + attw). The same checks run on
every PR via `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Generated artifacts (`platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
`platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, web-components `src/generated/`) are
gitignored and reproduced on build.

## Deliberate boundaries

- **canvas-ios and canvas-android get no dedicated targets** — both already self-generate from InstUI
  through their own Style Dictionary pipelines. pantoken's generic swift/android/compose cover the
  general native case; duplicating their in-repo scripts would drift.
- **Storybook is a renderer, not a design tool** — pantoken themes the Storybook _app_; it doesn't
  author design variables (that's Figma). The test is "theming the app" vs "providing
  design-authoring assets."
- **Go was declined** — no real Go UI consumer worth a target.

Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo gh/owner/name
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo et/project/repo
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
                 (positional, --checkpoint, or --commit) and a checkpoint that
                 has been pushed. A commit SHA is resolved to its checkpoint
                 by that repo's Entire API, so prefixes cannot be used here.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied,
                   including its subagent task records under "tasks".
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --task           With --transcript, stream a subagent's stored transcript
                   instead, selected by tool_use_id or agent_id (as listed
                   under "tasks" in --json).
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint. This is the only
                part of this command that writes: it stores the summary on the
                checkpoint and spends tokens with the configured summary
                provider. Every other mode only reads.
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

Usage:
  entire checkpoint explain [checkpoint-id | commit-sha] [flags]

Flags:
  -c, --checkpoint string             Explain a specific checkpoint (ID or prefix)
      --commit string                 Explain a specific commit (SHA or ref, "commit-ish")
      --force                         Regenerate summary even if one already exists (requires --generate)
      --full                          Show full parsed transcript (all prompts/responses)
      --generate                      Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
  -h, --help                          help for explain
      --insecure-http-auth            Allow plain-HTTP auth for --repo (local dev only)
      --json                          Output metadata as JSON (no transcript bytes)
      --limit int                     Cap the list view at N checkpoints (default: 100). Only meaningful with --json.
      --no-pager                      Disable pager output
      --raw-transcript                Show raw transcript file (JSONL format)
      --repo string                   Explain a checkpoint owned by another repo (gh/owner/name, et/project/repo, entire://<host>/gh/<owner>/<repo>, or entire://<host>/et/<project>/<repo>), read from that repo's Entire API
      --search-all                    Search all commits (no branch/depth limit, may be slow)
      --session string                Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)
      --session-index int             Session index within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based, defaults to latest) (default -1)
  -s, --short                         Show summary only (omit prompts and files)
      --summary-timeout-seconds int   Hard deadline in seconds for --generate summary generation; overrides summary_timeout_seconds setting. 0 = use setting; if setting is also unset or 0, no automatic deadline applies.

      --transcript                    Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes to stdout (a session's, or a subagent's with --task)

# A2UI first-class support in pantoken AI assets

## Goal

Make pantoken's consumer-facing AI guidance explicitly support using pantoken with A2UI. This is an `ai/` integration: it teaches coding agents how to select and apply pantoken tokens in A2UI clients. It does not add a pantoken renderer, platform target, design payload, protocol implementation, or runtime dependency.

## Rationale and boundaries

- A2UI v1.0 is a transport-agnostic streaming UI protocol. It delegates rendering and styling to framework-native client renderers and removes protocol-level theme properties.
- Official renderer SDKs cover React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose. Current A2UI docs list different protocol-version support by client (including Jetpack Compose at v0.9.1 while several other clients support v1.0); guidance must not imply parity.
- The web Basic Catalog is themed through documented `--a2ui-*` CSS custom properties. Agents should use verified pantoken tokens and current A2UI renderer guidance, not invent token names or assume every client uses CSS.
- Native consumers should use pantoken's existing Flutter, Compose, and Swift token outputs where appropriate. Do not introduce a duplicate A2UI token emitter.
- Keep A2UI protocol processing, transport code, custom catalog implementation, framework component rendering, and an A2UI-specific Figma/Design payload out of scope unless a concrete consumer need is established.

## Proposed implementation

1. **Define the guidance contract.** Describe A2UI as a supported integration context; explain the distinction between protocol/catalog, client renderer, transport, and visual theme. Give agents a short decision path based on the user's actual client framework and protocol version.
2. **Add reusable consumer guidance.** Update pantoken's shared consumer-facing `AGENTS.md` and `llms.txt` guidance with A2UI routing and token-use rules. These assets should identify when A2UI is relevant and route agents to the dedicated skill for implementation details.
3. **Use the repository's asset source pipeline.** The installable `@pantoken/ai` package and its evals live under `ai/pantoken-ai`, while canonical installable asset text is currently authored in `packages/scaffold/assets/` and `packages/scaffold/skills/`, then inlined by the scaffold generator. Make edits at the source of truth and ensure the generated assets flow through `@pantoken/ai`; do not hand-edit generated files.
4. **Add a dedicated installable skill.** Add a narrowly triggered `use-a2ui` skill with version-aware steps for integrating pantoken with A2UI clients. Register it in the asset generation/installation pipeline so it is available through `@pantoken/ai`.
5. **Add focused evaluations.** Add `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/use-a2ui` coverage for activation, framework-specific routing, reuse of existing pantoken packages, and negative cases that must not trigger the skill. Verify the skill's spec/eval alignment and stay within the configured token budget.
6. **Keep the package/docs story synchronized.** Update the `ai/pantoken-ai` README and package descriptions to advertise the new skill and shared A2UI guidance. Check whether both `@pantoken/ai` and `@pantoken/scaffold` releases need changesets based on which published outputs change.

## Expected source areas

- `packages/scaffold/assets/AGENTS.md`
- `packages/scaffold/assets/llms.txt`
- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/SKILL.md`
- `packages/scaffold/src/agent-assets.ts` and `packages/scaffold/scripts/generate.ts` (register and emit the skill)
- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/use-a2ui/` (focused trigger/behavior evaluations)
- `ai/pantoken-ai/README.md` and package metadata (describe the new installable skill)

## Verification and release

- Regenerate agent assets via the existing source script and verify generated output is current; do not edit generated output directly.
- Run the focused `@pantoken/scaffold` and `@pantoken/ai` checks/tests, including i18n drift checks where applicable.
- Run the A2UI Waza eval suite and skill spec verification.
- Run the repository's required publish checks and add changesets for every affected published package output. Do not add unrelated runtime dependencies.
- Confirm AI guidance covers the current A2UI docs while clearly marking per-client protocol-version differences.

## Decision

Implement both layers: shared guidance provides discovery and routing, while the dedicated `use-a2ui` skill provides the detailed, version-aware integration workflow. Keep them consistent and test both activation and non-activation through evals.

## Goal

Publish a reusable, versioned A2UI catalog that constrains agents to Pantoken-style components.

duplicate component implementations.

## Confirmed decisions

- Catalog coverage is complete: every public component record is in scope. Include missing mappings
  for supported clients rather than silently excluding components; utilities and declarations are
  not catalog components unless an existing renderer exposes them as one.
- Client coverage is all currently supported A2UI renderer SDKs. The current A2UI client guide lists
  React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose; verify each SDK's status and supported
  protocol version before implementation.
- Ship thin registration adapters in existing renderers as needed, in addition to the reusable
  catalog artifact. Keep catalog definitions and agent assets under `ai/`.
- Extend the A2UI Basic Catalog rather than replacing its standard layout vocabulary. Use a
  versioned `catalogId`, and publish protocol-specific catalog forms only where client compatibility
  requires them.

## Proposed approach

1. **Inventory coverage and contracts.** Map each public component record to its existing renderer
   implementations, property/modifier schema, child/slot rules, icons, events/actions, and
   accessibility behavior. Map the six A2UI SDKs to their actual catalog registration APIs and
   protocol versions. Build a component-by-client coverage matrix and identify missing glue.
2. **Define one source of truth.** Add a versioned Pantoken catalog definition in
   `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`. Generate its component schemas from existing metadata and renderer
   contracts where possible; add metadata at the canonical source when a component lacks enough
   schema information. Include only defined Pantoken components and functions, with typed properties,
   children, events, and icon requirements.
3. **Add thin client registrations.** For each supported A2UI SDK, adapt the catalog entries to the
   existing Pantoken renderer APIs. Reuse component rendering, property conversion, icon resolution,
   and behavior/event handlers; do not copy those implementations. Keep framework dependencies
   optional and isolated to the relevant adapter entry points.
4. **Distribute the agent contract.** Include catalog JSON/schema, component guidance, and client

content.text: what are the pros and cons of adding a2ui registration adapters to every renderer vs an a2ui renderer package that reexports the other packages with the registration data added?

input.message:
**Per-renderer adapters** fit each client’s native API and keep dependencies optional; tests and releases stay beside the renderer. The tradeoff is repeated A2UI registration glue and version coordination across React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Compose.

**A dedicated package that re-exports every renderer** offers one install/import point and one place for catalog tests. But it couples unrelated framework dependencies, can make installs and bundles larger, and still needs separate runtime bindings: one JavaScript package cannot natively re-export Dart, Swift, and Kotlin implementations. That also cuts across pantoken’s consumption-based package boundaries and its practice of keeping heavier integrations out of the eager umbrella entry point ([architecture overview](/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/architecture/overview.md)).

**My recommendation:** keep the versioned catalog/schema and generator in `ai/`, then add the thinnest adapters alongside existing renderers. If one package entry point is important, make it a small adapter package per language/runtime—or a web-only package with framework subpaths—not a blanket re-export of all renderers. Which direction should the plan take?

not auto-merge with dependency updates. Raw token families and source directories determine
ownership: token-only components go to `plugins/pantoken/custom-components`; existing canonical
components, such as Card, retain their owner under `formats/components`.

Stable token names follow changed upstream references through the existing core resolver when
registration and target evidence agree. Ambiguous changes list their before/after references and
themes for manual mapping review. A failed version-pinned InstUI export lookup is itself reported;
automation never treats a token's existence as proof of upstream component availability.

For promotions, the draft includes an unapplied patch moving the custom CSS into the canonical
component directory and replacing the custom function with a functional deprecated forwarder,
following `cardRules` and `cardCss`. The patch records the upstream adoption and alias retirement
boundaries. Registry order, exports, focused drift tests, guides, demos, browser verification, and
actual InstUI parity remain mandatory human-reviewed work before applying and merging it.

## Linting CSS

Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core CSS rules; anchor-positioning props are ignored and
`@scope` is allowed. `lint:cssdoc` runs `@cssdoc/cli` with `--max-warnings 0` over the same
web-components sources and generated components CSS, making it the single cssdoc lint instance.
Stylelint remains because the CLI covers doc hygiene, not the 24 core CSS correctness rules.

## The docs site

There are three site builds, and they exist for different jobs:

| Script              | Locale API | Where it runs                   | Why                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docs:build`        | English    | CI, every PR and main push      | A fast breakage check. Sets `DOCS_ROOT_LOCALE_ONLY=1`, so `<locale>/api/**` is excluded. |
| `docs:build:deploy` | All        | The `Deploy docs` workflow only | What ships. Deterministic `glossary` adapter — no AI, no network.                        |
| `docs:build:all`    | All        | Local                           | `docs:build:deploy` plus `docs:check:locales` (the parity gate).                         |

`docs:build` renders a site whose non-root locales have no API tree, so under
`DOCS_ROOT_LOCALE_ONLY=1` `config.ts` points every localized API nav link, sidebar route, and home-hero
action at the English `/api/` tree instead of a route it didn't build. Don't remove that fallback —
it's what keeps the English-only build internally consistent.

**Deploys are diff-scoped.** `Deploy docs` can run from three paths: a docs-affecting push to `main`,
the `Release` workflow's publish path via its `docs-deploy-request` marker artifact, or a manual
`workflow_dispatch`. The workflow first runs `docs/scripts/changed-pages.ts` against the selected base
ref. Page-scoped guide/API/home changes can render through `docs:build:deploy:partial`; global inputs
(VitePress config/theme, docs scripts, public assets, shared component/token/plugin sources, lockfile,
and deleted pages) fall back to the full `docs:build:deploy` route. Manual dispatches default to the
full build unless a base ref is supplied.

Partial deploy builds write VitePress output to `docs/.vitepress/partial-dist`, then overlay that onto
a restored complete `docs/.vitepress/dist` cache before preparing the deploy. If the full dist cache
is missing, a partial candidate falls back to the full docs build. The deploy workflow builds the site
itself; CI no longer uploads a `docs-site` artifact.

**The site deploys as a static site tree plus an asset bucket behind an edge router.** The
full-locale site is ~42k pages / ~138k files / ~3.8 GB, which is past the size, timeout, and
per-directory file caps of typical static hosts. The deploy workflow splits the output via
`docs/scripts/prepare-deploy.ts`, which also fails the deploy if the static tree exceeds 100,000
files or any file exceeds 25 MiB:

- **Static site tree** (`docs/.vitepress/deploy-site`): HTML pages (44 locales), root files (`sitemap.xml`, `hashmap.json`, `robots.txt`, `favicon.*`, `llms.txt`), and shadcn registry files (`/r/*`) (~43k files).
- **Asset bucket** (`docs/.vitepress/deploy-assets`): High-volume hashed client bundles (`/assets/*`) and demo assets (`/demos-assets/*`) (~95k files), synced via `docs/scripts/sync-assets.ts`. Only changed objects upload.
- **Edge router** (`docs/edge/src/index.ts`, configured by `docs/edge/wrangler.jsonc`): Routes `/assets/*` and `/demos-assets/*` to the bucket with immutable caching headers (`public, max-age=31536000, immutable`) and falls back to the static site tree for HTML and root documents. Deploy needs the `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` secrets; `DOCS_ASSETS_BUCKET` and `DOCS_ASSETS_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY` are optional repo variables.

**The deploy build is memory-bound.** Three settings keep it inside a 16 GB runner, and all three
have a reason:

- `themeConfig.search.options._render` skips `<locale>/api/**`. The local-search plugin runs a

The plan’s biggest problem is that the native adapters can’t “reuse existing Pantoken renderers”, because there aren’t any to reuse. Otherwise the structure holds up.

### Blocking
**1. Flutter, SwiftUI, and Compose have no component renderers.**

- `platforms/flutter`, `platforms/swift`, and `platforms/compose` each contain a single src/index.ts. They generate token constants (see the compose README: “numeric constants… reference them straight from composables”).
- Steps 3 and 5 and the “complete coverage” decision assume there’s something to wrap, and there isn’t.
- “Cover every component on every client” would mean writing and maintaining native Pantoken UI kits in Dart, Swift, and Kotlin. That’s a large new product, and it contradicts the stated “no duplicate implementations” goal.
- Decision for you: either (a) scope v1 to web, which covers React, Lit, and Angular through the web-component bridge, and ship native catalog-schema support only, or (b) make the native kits an explicit separate project.
- Recommendation: (a). On native, agents would use the Basic Catalog themed by the existing token output, which is what `use-a2ui` does today. The catalog JSON stays client-agnostic, and the coverage matrix marks native as “schema only”.

### Should fix
**2. Verify the A2UI facts before you commit to the design.** The plan states the Universal Web Components contract, the six-SDK list, and “extend the Basic Catalog” as fact. A pre-implementation check should confirm:

- Whether Universal Web Components actually register across React, Lit, and Angular in the shipped SDK versions.
- Which protocol versions each SDK supports. The current skill targets v1.0, and the plan hedges “verify each SDK’s status”.
- Whether catalogs can extend the Basic Catalog by reference or must copy it.
Make this a gating step zero with a written finding. The bridge design depends on the answers.

**3. Step 2 understates schema generation.** `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented (modifiers, aliases, `@scope`). A2UI components need typed props, child slots, and events. Part of that is likely missing, and the plan only says “add metadata where needed”. Spike two or three components first (for example Button, Tabs, Tooltip) to see how much new canonical metadata you need. Then adjust the scope and the coverage claim.

**4. Security belongs up front, not in step 7.** A catalog lets an LLM drive the UI, which gives you new input surfaces:

- Agent-supplied icon names, URLs, and HTML or slot content.
- Actions and functions that fire events.
- Attribute-to-property mapping on custom elements, which risks `innerHTML` or `href` injection.
Define an allowlist-only prop schema, ban raw HTML props, and add negative tests, before building the bridge. That also fits the Node-free runtime rule in `CLAUDE.md` for `@pantoken/web-components`.

**5. The bridge could import server-only packages.** The thin adapter lives in `renderers/web-components`, so it must not pull in `@cssdoc/*` or the generator. Say so in the plan, and keep the generator in `ai/` as a build script only.

### Smaller notes

- **Versioning.** Define the `catalogId` scheme and what counts as a breaking change. Removing a component or prop is breaking; adding one is additive. Without this, agents holding an old catalog break silently.
- **Drift gate.** You have the instui upgrade pipeline and a deprecation ledger. Tie catalog regeneration to them so an upstream bump can’t change the catalog without a version bump.
- **Docs browser.** Reusing the shadcn browser’s search patterns is fine. Drop “registration snippets” for native clients, since there’s no native registration to show.
- **Tests and evals.** Add negative evals (an agent inventing a non-catalog component), not only routing. The existing `use-a2ui` evals cover token theming, so keep those routing cases to avoid regressions.
- **Skill update.** The current `use-a2ui` skill says to use a custom catalog “only when the user explicitly requests one”. Revise that sentence deliberately once the catalog ships, or agents will keep ignoring it.
- **Sequencing.** The plan is one big change across about eight areas. Split it into milestones, each independently shippable with its own changeset: (1) verification and schema spike, (2) catalog source and generator, (3) web bridge, (4) docs browser, (5) native, if it’s still in scope.
- **Housekeeping.** The last line says the checkout is `main` with no changes, but you’re on `a2ui` with two commits already. The plan should record that those commits cover the skill and guidance only.

# @pantoken/compose

Emit Instructure design tokens as a Jetpack Compose (Kotlin) object, via Style Dictionary. It's the
modern Android counterpart to `@pantoken/android`'s resource XML: it flattens the token IR to
concrete, single-mode values and keeps the natively-typed tokens (colours, dimensions, numbers).

## Install

```sh
npm i @pantoken/compose
```

## Usage

```ts
import { generateCompose } from "@pantoken/compose";

const file = await generateCompose({
  outDir: "./app/src/main/kotlin",
  theme: "rebrand",
  className: "PanTokens", // the generated Kotlin object name (default)
});
```

Or via the CLI:

```sh
pantoken generate compose --out ./app/src/main/kotlin
pantoken generate compose --out ./app/src/main/kotlin --theme canvas --class BrandTokens
```

## Output

A single Kotlin file (named after `className`) declaring a Compose object of `Color`, `Dp`, and
numeric constants. Reference them straight from composables. Use this for Compose UIs; for the
Android View-system (XML) resources, use `@pantoken/android`.

## Compatibility

`vp run @pantoken/compose#check:compatibility` compiles the generated token object with Kotlin 2.1.10,
Compose UI 1.8.2, Android Gradle Plugin 8.9.2, Gradle 8.14.2, and Android API 35. This verifies
compile-time compatibility, not runtime rendering on a device.

## API

- **`generateCompose(options): Promise<string>`** — emit Kotlin for a named theme (from the vendored
  `@pantoken/tokens` IR). Returns the written file path.
- **`toCompose(tokens, options): Promise<string>`** — same, but for an explicit token IR. Returns
  the written file path.
- **`GenerateComposeOptions`** — the `outDir`, `theme`, `mode`, and `className` options both take.

## Related

- Pairs with `@pantoken/android` for the Android View-system (XML) counterpart.
- Uses `@pantoken/tokens` for the vendored token IR and `@pantoken/sd-config` for the Style
  Dictionary platforms.

## License

MIT

# Use pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines pantoken with an A2UI renderer. Pantoken supplies
design tokens and icons; A2UI supplies the UI protocol and framework-specific renderers. For
token-only work, reuse the installed A2UI renderer rather than adding a runtime, transport, renderer,
or custom catalog.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve pantoken, or
generic pantoken styling without A2UI. Use it for custom catalogs only when the user explicitly
requests one.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Identify the actual A2UI
renderer, its protocol version, and how the host framework applies themes. Check the current
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/) rather than assuming all
frameworks support the same protocol version or styling API. A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the
renderer; don't put theme properties in v1.0 protocol messages.

## 2. Apply pantoken to the existing renderer

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read
  the installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use
  pantoken's `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching,
  correctly typed token from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined.
  Keep the mapping scoped when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code color values or
  invent A2UI or InstUI property names.
- **Native clients:** Use pantoken's existing target output for the host: `pantoken generate
  flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's native theme API;
  CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- **Other web frameworks:** Choose the matching official A2UI renderer first, then use its supported
  theming mechanism. Don't assume React-specific setup applies to Lit or Angular.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; only add a custom component when
  the user asks for one.

## 3. Extend only when requested

If the user asks for a custom A2UI catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. A catalog defines agent-facing components and functions; pantoken tokens don't implement those
components or behaviors. Preserve the renderer's accessibility, focus, and interaction contracts.
Handle protocol transports only when explicitly in scope.

## 4. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference exists in the
installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI renderer version.

## References

- [A2UI v1.0 protocol](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)
- [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)
- [A2UI client integration](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/)
- [A2UI catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/)

# pantoken

Instructure design tokens and icons, reshaped for every platform. pantoken resolves Instructure UI's
tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then emits many small, individually-publishable
packages — CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus, React/Vue/Svelte, Tailwind/Panda, native Swift/Kotlin, WordPress,
Figma, and more — unified by an unscoped `pantoken` meta package.

Read `README.md` for the consumer quickstart. This file is the map to everything an agent needs; open
the linked docs only when a task calls for them.

## How to work here

- **Use the `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` CLIs — never raw pnpm, npm, or yarn.** They're global bins. Package
  scripts must never shell out to `pnpm` internally: CI provides `vp` but not `pnpm` on PATH, so a
  `pnpm run …` inside a script breaks the docs deploy. Details in `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start.** "Port in use" is not "stale" — the user runs their own
  dev servers in other windows. For your own preview server, bind a distinct port with `--strictPort`.
  If a port is taken, pick another or ask.
- **Decide one fork at a time.** Give a recommendation plus the tradeoff, then let the user choose.
  Verify third-party claims (upstream token names, browser support, a library's capability) before
  asserting them.
- **Writing:** active voice, contractions, plain language, Oxford comma. Don't use empowering,
  harnessing, unlocking, supercharging, transforming, game-changing, seamless, robust, leverage, or
  synergy.
- **Keep `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/web-components` runtime graphs Node-free** — they ship
  to the browser. A value import of a postcss-based `@cssdoc/*` package pulls a `node:module` shim
  into the bundle and kills client JS. Type-only imports are fine; value imports belong in build
  scripts and tests.
- **Generate a changeset for every user-visible change.** Run `pnpm changeset` and commit the
  `.changeset/*.md` file alongside the code change.
- **When refining user-facing packages, evaluate `@pantoken/ai` in the same change.** If package
  recommendations, CLI target examples, or usage conventions changed, update the consumer agent assets
  in `ai/pantoken-ai` so assistant guidance does not drift.
- **Keep security docs current.** When a code change alters a threat, adds a control, or closes a
  residual risk in `ASSURANCE.md`, update both `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` before merging.

## Knowledge map

| When you need to…                                                                  | Read…                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Understand the monorepo, the pipeline, and why `@pantoken/model` exists            | `docs/architecture/overview.md`      |
| Author or extend a component (records, the modifier convention, aliases, `@scope`) | `docs/conventions/authoring.md`      |
| Work on the web components (shadow CSS, `register()`/prefix, the JS-behavior tier) | `docs/conventions/web-components.md` |
| Run more than one theme or color scheme in a single document                       | `docs/conventions/scoping.md`        |
| Build, lint, release, or work on the docs site + i18n + cssdoc integration         | `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` |
| Avoid re-solving a known bug or gotcha                                             | `docs/engineering-log.md`            |
| Amend the security assurance case after adding a new input surface or control      | `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`        |
| Match an agent to a domain                                                         | `AGENTS.md`                          |

## Repo shape

Organized by _how you consume_ each package: `packages/` core machinery · `formats/` importable
serializations (css, icons, scss, components, …) · `platforms/` generated foreign-ecosystem source ·
`renderers/` UI integrations (web-components, framework wrappers, bridges) · `bundlers/` build-pipeline
plugins · `design/` Figma + swatches · `plugins/{pantoken,postcss,typedoc,vite}/` · `tools/` internal
build tooling · `ai/` consumer-facing agent assets. The gate is `pnpm run ready` +
`pnpm run check:publish`.

# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI

## Goal

Publish a reusable, versioned A2UI catalog that constrains agents to Pantoken-style components.
Cover every public Pantoken component and every officially supported A2UI client, reusing existing
component renderers, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction behavior. Keep the canonical
catalog and agent-facing vocabulary in `ai/`, and make the catalog browsable on the docs site. Add
only thin A2UI registration adapters to existing renderer packages where their current APIs require
them. Do not create a new renderer package or duplicate component implementations.

## Confirmed decisions

- Catalog coverage is complete: every public component record is in scope. Include missing mappings
  for supported clients rather than silently excluding components; utilities and declarations are
  not catalog components unless an existing renderer exposes them as one.
- Client coverage is all currently supported A2UI renderer SDKs. The current A2UI client guide lists
  React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose; verify each SDK's status and supported
  protocol version before implementation.
- Ship thin registration adapters in existing renderers as needed, in addition to the reusable
  catalog artifact. Keep catalog definitions and agent assets under `ai/`.
- Prefer A2UI Universal Web Components for the React, Lit, and Angular clients: one web component
  implementation can register across all three. Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose still need
  native adapters.
- Include a searchable docs-site catalog with schemas, support information, raw JSON, and
  registration snippets; defer live component previews.
- Extend the A2UI Basic Catalog rather than replacing its standard layout vocabulary. Use a
  versioned `catalogId`, and publish protocol-specific catalog forms only where client compatibility
  requires them.

## Architecture decision

- Keep the versioned catalog, schema source, generator, and agent-facing vocabulary in `ai/`.
- Add only thin A2UI registration adapters alongside existing renderers, reusing their component
  rendering and behavior implementations.
- Do not add a blanket `@pantoken/a2ui` package that re-exports every renderer. That would couple
  unrelated dependencies and cannot provide one native runtime package for JavaScript, Dart, Swift,
  and Kotlin. If consumers later need a single import point, consider a web-only adapter package
  with framework subpaths or a small adapter package per runtime.

## Proposed approach

1. **Inventory coverage and contracts.** Map each public component record to its existing renderer
   implementations, property/modifier schema, child/slot rules, icons, events/actions, and
   accessibility behavior. Map the six A2UI SDKs to their actual catalog registration APIs and
   protocol versions. Build a component-by-client coverage matrix and identify missing glue.
2. **Define one source of truth.** Add a versioned Pantoken catalog definition in
   `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`. Generate its component schemas from existing metadata and renderer
   contracts where possible; add metadata at the canonical source when a component lacks enough
   schema information. Include only defined Pantoken components and functions, with typed properties,
   children, events, and icon requirements.
3. **Add client registrations.** For web, use A2UI's Universal Web Component contract to bridge
   existing `@pantoken/web-components` elements into one registration shared by React, Lit, and
   Angular. Reuse component rendering, property conversion, icon resolution, and behavior/event
   handlers; do not copy those implementations. Add native adapters for Flutter, SwiftUI, and
   Jetpack Compose, reusing their existing Pantoken renderers. Keep SDK dependencies optional and
   isolated to adapter entry points. See
   [A2UI Universal Web Components](https://a2ui.org/guides/authoring-universal-components/).
4. **Distribute the agent contract.** Include catalog JSON/schema, component guidance, and client
   registration examples in the published `@pantoken/ai` package. Update the canonical `use-a2ui`
   skill and relevant shared agent assets in `packages/scaffold` so agents select only registered
   Pantoken components, compose them with the Basic Catalog, and respect each SDK's version.
5. **Protect the contract from drift.** Generate and validate the catalog against all public
   component records and all supported client adapters. Add integration tests for properties,
   nested children, icons, events/functions, and accessible interactions, plus Waza evaluations that
   test constrained vocabulary and negative routing.
6. **Add a browsable catalog to the docs site.** Generate its data from the same catalog source of
   truth. Add an A2UI-specific VitePress browser with search/filter, component properties and
   children, events/functions, client support, raw JSON, and registration snippets. Reuse the
   shadcn browser's static-data and search patterns, but not its install commands or CSS previews.
   Localize the browser UI in English and Hungarian. Do not add a live A2UI runtime preview in this
   release.
7. **Update documentation and release gates.** Document installation, catalog registration, version
   compatibility, and extension points. Review security implications of exposing client functions
   or actions; update `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` if the catalog adds input surfaces or controls.
   Add changesets for each published package whose output changes.

## Expected source areas

- `formats/components/src/` — public component records and modifier metadata.
- `renderers/web-components/` — shared web A2UI Universal Component bridge over existing custom
  elements.
- Existing Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose renderer/platform packages — thin native A2UI
  registrations over existing implementations.
- `formats/interactions/src/` — reusable event and behavior contracts.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/`, and package metadata — catalog source,
  generated package assets, and published-file inclusion.
- `docs/scripts/`, `docs/a2ui/`, and `docs/.vitepress/theme/` — generated static catalog data,
  searchable browser, route, localization, and focused tests.
- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/` and `packages/scaffold/assets/` — installable skill and shared
  consumer guidance.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/` and existing renderer tests — catalog activation, coverage, and behavior.
- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, package documentation, and `.changeset/` — security and release
  updates when applicable.

## Verification

- Validate catalog JSON against the selected A2UI schemas and every client's supported protocol
  version; verify stable, versioned catalog IDs and Basic Catalog composition.
- Assert complete component-by-client coverage with no missing or duplicate component mappings.
- Verify the docs browser uses the generated catalog source, localizes its UI, and exposes the raw
  schema and registration information without introducing a second catalog definition.
- Run focused tests for every adapter and behavior, A2UI skill/eval checks, accessibility checks,
  `vp check`, relevant package tests, and publish checks.
- Verify consumer-facing package contents and add changesets. Keep the work on the existing `a2ui`
  branch; the current checkout is `main`, and no repository files have been changed in this planning
  phase.

+- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
+  child slots, and events is not established.
+- The official A2UI guidance currently documents Universal Web Components and Basic Catalog
+  composition. Compatibility still needs verification against the exact released SDK versions
+  selected for Pantoken; do not treat documentation for floating versions as the shipping contract.
+
+## Proposed scope and decisions to confirm
+
+- **Web-first v1:** support React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
+  over `@pantoken/web-components`, provided the version gate confirms the selected SDK contracts.
+- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
+  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
+  Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
+  not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.
+- **Catalog and package boundaries:** canonical catalog, generator, and agent guidance live in
+  `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
+  package that re-exports every renderer.
+- **Coverage claim:** first spike Button, Tabs, and Tooltip. After the spike, define the v1 set as
+  the A2UI-usable web components for which the source contract can accurately specify properties,
+  children, icons, and events. Do not promise every CSS record or claim complete coverage until a
+  coverage audit demonstrates it. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components unless a
+  real renderer exposes them as components.
+- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary and compose Pantoken-specific
+  components with it where supported.
+- **Docs:** add a searchable, browse-only catalog with schemas, support status, and raw JSON.
+  Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.
+
+## Architecture and safety constraints
+
+- Verify, before implementation, the released React/Lit/Angular A2UI SDK versions and their
+  Universal Web Component registration contract, supported protocol versions, and whether/how a
+  custom catalog composes with the Basic Catalog. Record the evidence and exact versions. If any
+  required contract is unavailable or incompatible, stop and revise the bridge design rather than
+  infer it.
+- The schema spike must identify the canonical source for typed properties, child/slot rules,
+  events/functions, icons, and accessibility behavior. Do not assume CSS modifier metadata supplies
+  these contracts. If substantial new metadata or renderer behavior is required, revise the coverage
+  and release scope before building the catalog.
+- Before bridge implementation, define a strict component and property allowlist; reject unknown
+  components and props, raw HTML/markup, unsafe URLs, unrecognized icon names, and arbitrary action
+  or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.
+  Add negative tests for rejected inputs.
+- Keep the runtime bridge browser-safe and Node-free. Do not import `@cssdoc/*`, catalog generators,
+  or other build-only code into `renderers/web-components`; generation belongs in `ai/` build
+  tooling.
+- Give the catalog a stable, immutable, versioned `catalogId` (a `/vN/` identity, not a mutable
+  `latest` URL). Treat component/prop removal, renames, required-prop changes, and incompatible
+  semantics as breaking; additions that preserve old messages are additive. Tie regeneration and
+  explicit version changes to the InstUI upgrade/deprecation workflow so upstream drift cannot
+  silently alter the published contract.
+- Update `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` if the catalog or bridge adds input surfaces or controls.
+
+## Milestones
+
+1. **Verification and schema/security spike.** Pin the relevant A2UI SDK versions and document
+   protocol, universal registration, and Basic Catalog findings. Inspect Button, Tabs, and Tooltip
+   across component records and web renderers; produce an initial coverage matrix and identify
+   missing canonical metadata. Specify the allowlist and negative security cases. This milestone is
+   a gate: revise or stop if the evidence does not support the proposed web bridge or scope.
+2. **Catalog contract and generator.** Add the canonical, versioned web catalog in `ai/`, generate
+   it from validated source metadata, and test schema validity, stable IDs, coverage, and drift.
+   Publish the catalog and appropriate agent guidance with a changeset for changed package output.
+3. **Universal web bridge.** Implement the thin A2UI Universal Web Component integration over
+   existing web components. Reuse existing property conversion, icon resolution, and behaviors;
+   add no native UI kit and no duplicated rendering implementation. Test allowlisted props, nested
+   children, events, icons, and rejected input.
+4. **Docs catalog browser.** Generate static browser data from the same catalog source. Reuse the
+   shadcn browser's search/static-data patterns, not its install commands or previews. Show
+   per-client support, schemas, props, children, actions, raw JSON, and web-only registration
+   examples; localize new UI in English and Hungarian.
+5. **Agent evaluations, release, and drift gates.** Keep existing A2UI token-theming evaluations.
+   Add positive web catalog routing and negative evaluations for invented components, invalid
+   properties, and unsupported native registration. Update `use-a2ui` so agents use the Pantoken
+   catalog for supported web clients and the Basic Catalog plus Pantoken tokens for native. Run
+   focused tests, security checks, package checks, and publish checks. Ship each independently
+   releasable package change with its changeset; follow repository release policy for docs-only
+   work.
+
+## Expected source areas
+
+- `formats/components/src/` and `renderers/web-components/src/` — source-contract audit and web
+  component behavior.
+- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/`, and package metadata — canonical catalog,
+  generation, published assets, and version/drift checks.
+- `renderers/web-components/` — thin Universal Web Component bridge, with no build-only imports.
+- `docs/scripts/`, `docs/a2ui/`, and `docs/.vitepress/theme/` — generated static data, browser,
+  routing, localization, and focused tests.
+- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/` and `packages/scaffold/assets/` — updated skill and shared
+  consumer guidance.
+- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/` and renderer tests — positive and negative agent/bridge behavior.
+- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, package documentation, and `.changeset/` — security and release
+  updates when applicable.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Record version-specific evidence for the selected A2UI SDKs, Universal Web Component support,
+  protocol compatibility, and Basic Catalog composition before implementation.
+- Use the Button/Tabs/Tooltip spike to validate schema-source sufficiency; gate any broader coverage
+  claim on the resulting audit.
+- Validate the generated catalog against the selected A2UI schema and assert its versioned ID,
+  allowlist, and drift behavior.
+- Test web registration and property/child/icon/event behavior, including unsafe/unknown inputs;
+  verify the browser runtime graph remains Node-free.
+- Verify the docs browser uses generated catalog data, localizes its UI, and labels native support
+  as schema-only without native registration examples.
+- Run existing and new A2UI Waza evaluations, focused package tests, `vp check`, and applicable
+  publish checks. Add changesets for package output and public behavior changes.
*** End Patch

import { buttonCss } from "@pantoken/components";
import type { ElementDefinition } from "../lib/context.ts";

/**
 * `<instui-button>` — a token-styled `<button>`. The `variant` attribute maps to the `-color-<variant>`
 * modifier (`secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `danger`, `ai`, …); `margin` adds spacing around the
 * host (InstUI keywords like `small` / `medium large`); slotted content is the label.
 *
 * It is also a native invoker: `popovertarget` (with optional `popovertargetaction`) toggles any
 * light-DOM `[popover]` such as `<instui-context-view>`, `<instui-popover>`, or `<instui-tray>`, and
 * `command`/`commandfor` drives the command-based components (`<instui-modal>` with `--show`/`--close`,
 * etc.). The id is forwarded to the inner button via the invoker IDL, so it resolves across the shadow
 * boundary and may point forward to an element declared later in the document.
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <instui-button variant="primary" margin="small">Save changes</instui-button>
 * <instui-button variant="danger" margin="small">Delete</instui-button>
 * <instui-button popovertarget="cv">Details</instui-button>
 * <instui-context-view id="cv">More about this item.</instui-context-view>
 * ```
 */
export const button: ElementDefinition = {
  name: "button",
  define: (ctx) =>
    ctx.wrapper(
      "instui-button",
      buttonCss(ctx.I),
      (host) =>
        `<button class="${ctx.variantClass("button", host)}" part="button"><slot></slot></button>`,
      { invoker: true },
    ),
};

Contents of https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/:
# SDKs

Official A2UI SDKs are organized into three layers:

*   **Core SDK** for shared protocol models and surface state.
*   **Agent SDK** for catalog-driven prompt generation and model output compilation.
*   **Renderer SDK** for mounting surface state in a client UI framework.

Both the Agent SDK and the Renderer SDK build on their language’s Core SDK, so server-side validation and client-side message resolution share one implementation per language. Client-server applications typically pair two layers on each side of a network boundary, such as a Python agent server communicating with a SwiftUI or Jetpack Compose client. Codebases that handle both model inference and UI rendering in the same language, such as TypeScript web apps or Dart and Flutter apps, can use all three layers together in one project.

## Core SDK

Every Agent SDK and Renderer SDK depends on its language’s Core SDK, which implements the protocol data structures, reactive state containers, and expression evaluators common to agents and clients.

### Primary functions

1.  Parses and serializes A2UI [wire messages](/concepts/messages/) across supported protocol versions (v1.0, v0.9.1, and v0.8 in TypeScript and Python).
2.  Loads [Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) JSON Schemas and validates component hierarchies, placement constraints, and message payloads.
3.  Maintains per-surface component graphs and JSON [data model](/concepts/data-binding/) state while applying incremental updates by component ID and JSON Pointer path.
4.  Evaluates data bindings, collection templates, string interpolation expressions, function invocations, and validation checks.

### Packages

| Language   | Published packages                                                                                                                                           | Versions           | Source                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript | [@a2ui/web\_core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/web_core)                                                                                              | v0.8, v0.9.1, v1.0 | [typescript/core/web\_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/core/web_core) |
| Python     | [a2ui-core](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-core/)                                                                                                             | v0.8, v0.9.1, v1.0 | [python/a2ui\_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_core)                 |
| Dart       | [a2ui\_core](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_core)                                                                                                             | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [dart/a2ui\_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/dart/a2ui_core)                     |
| Swift      | [A2UISwiftCore](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift)   [BasicCatalog](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift) | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [swift/core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/swift/core)                              |
| Kotlin     | [androidx.a2ui](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/a2ui)                                                                                | v0.9.1             | [AndroidX a2ui](https://cs.android.com/androidx/platform/frameworks/support/+/androidx-main:a2ui/)   |

All v0.9.1 packages accept v0.9 wire envelopes and catalog IDs. Swift packages are distributed through Swift Package Manager from [`a2ui-project/a2ui`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui) (the `A2UISwiftCore` product exposes the `A2UICore` module), and the AndroidX group on Google Maven publishes the `a2ui-model` and `a2ui-engine` artifacts.

Most applications install a Core SDK automatically through an [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) or [Renderer SDK](#renderer-sdk), though you can depend on a Core SDK directly to build headless state processors or custom UI adapters. To implement a Core SDK in another language, read [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules) and validate against the YAML suites in [`conformance/core`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/core).

## Agent SDK

An Agent SDK connects a language model or agent runtime to the A2UI protocol while leaving model selection, tool execution, and conversation state under your application’s control.

### Primary functions

1.  Negotiates active [Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) definitions and protocol versions (v0.9.1 and v1.0) against the capabilities reported by the client renderer (see [Overview](/concepts/overview/)).
2.  Generates skills, system prompt instructions, and examples directly from catalog schemas and prompt instructions, replacing hand-written prompts that become outdated when components change.
3.  Compiles streaming or batch model output from [inference formats](/concepts/inference-formats/) (such as compact Express syntax, which cuts output tokens without client changes, or chunk-healed Direct JSON) into standard A2UI [wire messages](/concepts/messages/).
4.  Validates outgoing messages statefully against active surface state on the server so broken component IDs, placement violations, or schema mismatches can be fed back to the model for self-correction before transmission.
5.  Supports optional server-side [`@macro`](/guides/macros/) expansion in Python and integrates with agent frameworks and transports including [Google ADK](https://github.com/google/adk-python) and the [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/).

### Packages

| Language   | Published packages                                                                                                                                                       | Versions           | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript | [@a2ui/agent](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/agent)                                                                                                                 | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [typescript/agents/a2ui\_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/agents/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                                                     |
| Python     | [a2ui-agent-sdk](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-agent-sdk/)   [a2ui-adk](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-adk/) (ADK)   [a2ui-a2a](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-a2a/) (A2A) | v0.8, v0.9.1, v1.0 | [python/a2ui\_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_agent)   [python/a2ui\_adk](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_adk)   [python/a2ui\_a2a](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_a2a) |
| Dart       | [a2ui\_agent](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                       | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [dart/a2ui\_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/dart/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                                                                               |

Swift and Kotlin target client-side rendering; for legacy v0.8 and v0.9 JVM servers, [`kotlin/agent_sdk_legacy`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/kotlin/agent_sdk_legacy) remains in the repository.

### Go and community SDKs

For **Go** services and CLI clients, community-maintained libraries cover server-side validation, streaming parsers, and terminal rendering—including [`satorunooshie/a2ui-go`](https://github.com/satorunooshie/a2ui-go), [`tmc/a2ui`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/tmc/a2ui), [`charmbracelet/a2tea`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/a2tea), and [`muncus/a2term`](https://github.com/muncus/a2term) (listed with version details in [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/)).

To implement a conformance-verified Core or Agent SDK in Go, Rust, C#, or another language, follow the language-agnostic specifications in [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules), verify behavioral parity against the YAML suites in [`conformance/core`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/core) and [`conformance/agent`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/agent), and open a pull request to add your package to [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/#how-to-submit-a-project).

See [Using a catalog in an agent](/concepts/catalogs/#using-a-catalog-in-an-agent) and [Inference Formats](/concepts/inference-formats/#how-inference-formats-stay-swappable) for TypeScript, Python, and Dart examples of configuring `A2uiGenerator`, negotiating capabilities, and compiling model responses, or run a working agent in the [Quickstart](/quickstart/).

## Renderer SDK

A Renderer SDK connects a Core SDK’s resolved surface state to a client UI framework. Official Renderer SDKs include a built-in implementation of the [Basic Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/#the-basic-catalog) styled through the host framework’s theming system, and let you register custom catalogs with per-component rendering logic and local functions (see [How to Define a Catalog](/guides/defining-a-catalog/)).

### Primary functions

1.  Applies incremental [surface, component, and data model updates](/concepts/messages/) across supported protocol versions (v0.9.1, v1.0, and v0.8 on Web), updating only changed subtrees so unchanged siblings keep focus and local UI state.
2.  Evaluates [reactive data bindings](/concepts/data-binding/), nested collection scopes, relative JSON Pointers, and local two-way input edits.
3.  Executes [local catalog functions](/concepts/catalogs/#functions) and [reactive validation checks](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#component-validation--check-rules), enforcing v1.0 caller and user-activation rules.
4.  Builds capability and data-model sync metadata payloads for your transport layer, dispatches user action events and structured error messages, and handles v1.0 bidirectional function RPCs.
5.  Maps protocol accessibility attributes to host accessibility APIs across Flutter, Web WAI-ARIA, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose.

### Packages

| Framework       | Published packages                                                                                                                                                                          | Versions           | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
