name: use-a2ui
description: Inspect an app's installed A2UI renderer and apply pantoken tokens or icons through its supported theme API. Use for A2UI renderer theming or native token output, not transport-only or generic pantoken tasks.
---

# Use pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines pantoken with an A2UI renderer. Pantoken supplies
design tokens and icons; A2UI supplies the UI protocol and framework-specific renderers. For
token-only work, reuse the installed A2UI renderer rather than adding a runtime, transport, renderer,
or custom catalog.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve pantoken, or
generic pantoken styling without A2UI. Use it for custom catalogs only when the user explicitly
requests one.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Identify the actual A2UI
renderer, its protocol version, and how the host framework applies themes. Check the current
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/) rather than assuming all
frameworks support the same protocol version or styling API. A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the
renderer; don't put theme properties in v1.0 protocol messages.

## 2. Apply pantoken to the existing renderer

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read
  the installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use
  pantoken's `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching,
  correctly typed token from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined.
  Keep the mapping scoped when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code color values or
  invent A2UI or InstUI property names.
- **Native clients:** Use pantoken's existing target output for the host: `pantoken generate
  flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's native theme API;
  CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- **Other web frameworks:** Choose the matching official A2UI renderer first, then use its supported
  theming mechanism. Don't assume React-specific setup applies to Lit or Angular.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; only add a custom component when
  the user asks for one.

## 3. Extend only when requested

If the user asks for a custom A2UI catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. A catalog defines agent-facing components and functions; pantoken tokens don't implement those
components or behaviors. Preserve the renderer's accessibility, focus, and interaction contracts.
Handle protocol transports only when explicitly in scope.

## 4. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference exists in the
installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI renderer version.

## References

- [A2UI v1.0 protocol](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)
- [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)
- [A2UI client integration](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/)
- [A2UI catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/)

See [Registering a catalog in a renderer](/concepts/catalogs/#registering-a-catalog-in-a-renderer) and [How to Define a Catalog](/guides/defining-a-catalog/) for Flutter, Web, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose examples of setting up a message processor, registering component widgets and local functions, and mounting surfaces, or run a React or Flutter client in the [Quickstart](/quickstart/). Read [Authoring Universal Web Components](/guides/authoring-universal-components/) to share custom components across React, Lit, and Angular, or see the [Android Jetpack Compose guide](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/agentic) for Android integration. Browse [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/) for community renderers, or consult [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules) and [`conformance`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance) to build a custom framework adapter.

# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI

## Goal

Publish a versioned A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary,
using Pantoken's existing web-component rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction
behavior where those contracts exist. Keep the canonical catalog and agent-facing material in
`ai/`. Do not create native Pantoken UI kits or duplicate component implementations as part of this
work.

## Current state

- Work is on the existing `a2ui` branch. Its two existing commits add the A2UI skill and shared agent
  guidance; catalog implementation has not started.
- Flutter, Swift, and Compose currently emit design-token constants, not Pantoken component
  renderers. There is no native UI implementation to adapt.
- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
  child slots, and events is not established.
- The A2UI Universal Web Components guide documents a Zod `ComponentApi` plus
  `A2uiLitElement`/`WebComponentImplementation`, and says the host renderers register these
  implementations. The latest published packages checked are `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0,
  `@a2ui/react` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/lit` 0.15.0, and `@a2ui/angular` 0.14.0.
- The published React 0.15.0 and Angular 0.14.0 renderer bundles use
  `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9/universal`; Lit 0.15.0 exposes the universal element API and a v0.9 entry.
  The SDK overview lists v1.0 support for these frameworks, but the shipped Universal Component
  path for React and Angular is versioned to v0.9. This does not yet establish a common v1.0
  Universal Component contract across all three.
- A2UI v1.0 documentation shows Basic Catalog components being reused in a custom `Catalog` and
  allows a component to identify a second catalog with `@catalogId`. The v0.9.1 guide says a
  surface binds to a single `catalogId`, so the web client must register a combined Basic +
  Pantoken catalog; its exact catalog/agent composition API remains to be pinned.
- The schema spike confirms that the CSS component records do not define typed A2UI properties,
  child slots, or actions. Button's web-element contract is only described in JSDoc; Tabs requires
  a coordinated tablist/tab/panel structure and keyboard behavior; Tooltip has `tip`, `placement`,
  delays, and slotted trigger content, with text content rendered safely via `textContent`.
  Therefore full catalog coverage is not established by existing metadata. The coverage audit
  must decide which components can be supported without inventing undocumented behavior.

## Confirmed scope and decisions

- **Web-first v1:** support React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
  over `@pantoken/web-components`, provided the version gate confirms the selected SDK contracts.
  The user confirmed this boundary.
- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
  Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
  not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.
- **Catalog and package boundaries:** canonical catalog, generator, and agent guidance live in
  `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
  package that re-exports every renderer.
- **Coverage claim:** first spike Button, Tabs, and Tooltip. After the spike, define the v1 set as
  the A2UI-usable web components for which the source contract can accurately specify properties,
  children, icons, and events. Do not promise every CSS record or claim complete coverage until a
  coverage audit demonstrates it. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components unless a
  real renderer exposes them as components.
- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary and compose Pantoken-specific
  components with it where supported.
- **Protocol remains a gate decision:** either target the currently evident common Universal
  Component path (v0.9.1, with a merged Basic + Pantoken catalog), or keep v1.0 and wait for or add
  compatible framework-specific registration. Do not silently mix the v1.0 catalog contract with
  renderers whose released Universal path is v0.9.
- **Docs:** add a searchable, browse-only catalog with schemas, support status, and raw JSON.
  Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.

## Architecture and safety constraints

- Verify, before implementation, the released React/Lit/Angular A2UI SDK versions and their
  Universal Web Component registration contract, supported protocol versions, and whether/how a
  custom catalog composes with the Basic Catalog. Record the evidence and exact versions. If any
  required contract is unavailable or incompatible, stop and revise the bridge design rather than
  infer it.
- The schema spike must identify the canonical source for typed properties, child/slot rules,
  events/functions, icons, and accessibility behavior. Do not assume CSS modifier metadata supplies
  these contracts. If substantial new metadata or renderer behavior is required, revise the coverage
  and release scope before building the catalog.
- Before bridge implementation, define a strict component and property allowlist; reject unknown
  components and props, raw HTML/markup, unsafe URLs, unrecognized icon names, and arbitrary action
  or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.
  Add negative tests for rejected inputs.
- Keep the runtime bridge browser-safe and Node-free. Do not import `@cssdoc/*`, catalog generators,
  or other build-only code into `renderers/web-components`; generation belongs in `ai/` build
  tooling.

# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI

## Goal

Publish a versioned A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary,
using Pantoken's existing web-component rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction
behavior where those contracts exist. Keep the canonical catalog and agent-facing material in
`ai/`. Do not create native Pantoken UI kits or duplicate component implementations as part of this
work.

## Current state

- Work is on the existing `a2ui` branch. Its two existing commits add the A2UI skill and shared agent
  guidance; catalog implementation has not started.
- Flutter, Swift, and Compose currently emit design-token constants, not Pantoken component
  renderers. There is no native UI implementation to adapt.
- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
  child slots, and events is not established.
- The A2UI Universal Web Components guide documents a Zod `ComponentApi` plus
  `A2uiLitElement`/`WebComponentImplementation`, and says the host renderers register these
  implementations. The latest published packages checked are `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0,
  `@a2ui/react` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/lit` 0.15.0, and `@a2ui/angular` 0.14.0.
- The published React 0.15.0 and Angular 0.14.0 renderer bundles use
  `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9/universal`; Lit 0.15.0 exposes the universal element API and a v0.9 entry.
  The SDK overview lists v1.0 support for these frameworks, but the shipped Universal Component
  path for React and Angular is versioned to v0.9. This does not yet establish a common v1.0
  Universal Component contract across all three.
- A2UI v1.0 documentation shows Basic Catalog components being reused in a custom `Catalog` and
  allows a component to identify a second catalog with `@catalogId`. The v0.9.1 guide says a
  surface binds to a single `catalogId`, so the web client must register a combined Basic +
  Pantoken catalog; its exact catalog/agent composition API remains to be pinned.
- The schema spike confirms that the CSS component records do not define typed A2UI properties,
  child slots, or actions. Button's web-element contract is only described in JSDoc; Tabs requires
  a coordinated tablist/tab/panel structure and keyboard behavior; Tooltip has `tip`, `placement`,
  delays, and slotted trigger content, with text content rendered safely via `textContent`.
  Therefore full catalog coverage is not established by existing metadata. The coverage audit
  must decide which components can be supported without inventing undocumented behavior.

  over `@pantoken/web-components`, using protocol v0.9.1, the common Universal path evident in the
  current published React and Angular packages. Do not claim v1.0 Universal support; add it only in
  a separate follow-up after the released framework SDK contract is verified.
- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.

# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI

## Goal

Publish a versioned A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary,
using Pantoken's existing web-component rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction
behavior where those contracts exist. Keep the canonical catalog and agent-facing material in
`ai/`. Do not create native Pantoken UI kits or duplicate component implementations as part of this
work.

## Current state

- Work is on the existing `a2ui` branch. Its two existing commits add the A2UI skill and shared agent
  guidance; catalog implementation has not started.
- Flutter, Swift, and Compose currently emit design-token constants, not Pantoken component
  renderers. There is no native UI implementation to adapt.
- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
  child slots, and events is not established.
- The A2UI Universal Web Components guide documents a Zod `ComponentApi` plus
  `A2uiLitElement`/`WebComponentImplementation`, and says the host renderers register these
  implementations. The latest published packages checked are `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0,
  `@a2ui/react` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/lit` 0.15.0, and `@a2ui/angular` 0.14.0.
- The published React 0.15.0 and Angular 0.14.0 renderer bundles use
  `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9/universal`; Lit 0.15.0 exposes the universal element API and a v0.9 entry.
  The SDK overview lists v1.0 support for these frameworks, but the shipped Universal Component
  path for React and Angular is versioned to v0.9. This does not yet establish a common v1.0
  Universal Component contract across all three; do not infer v1.0 compatibility from the overview
  alone.
- A2UI v1.0 documentation shows Basic Catalog components being reused in a custom `Catalog` and
  allows a component to identify a second catalog with `@catalogId`. The v0.9.1 guide says a
  surface binds to a single `catalogId`, so the web client must register a combined Basic +
  Pantoken catalog; its exact catalog/agent composition API remains to be pinned.
- The schema spike confirms that the CSS component records do not define typed A2UI properties,
  child slots, or actions. Button's web-element contract is only described in JSDoc; Tabs requires
  a coordinated tablist/tab/panel structure and keyboard behavior; Tooltip has `tip`, `placement`,
  delays, and slotted trigger content, with text content rendered safely via `textContent`.
  Therefore full catalog coverage is not established by existing metadata. The coverage audit
  must decide which components can be supported without inventing undocumented behavior.

## Confirmed scope and decisions

- **Protocol:** use A2UI 1.0 only, as directed. Do not downgrade to 0.9.
- **Web-first v1:** target React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
  over `@pantoken/web-components` only after exact released SDK versions prove v1.0 support. The
  latest React/Angular packages checked do not yet establish that contract.
- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
  Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
  not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.
- **Catalog and package boundaries:** canonical catalog, generator, and agent guidance live in
  `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
  package that re-exports every renderer.
- **Coverage claim:** the initial catalog supports Button and Tooltip with explicit allowlisted
  schemas. Defer Tabs and other elements until each has an authored typed contract; Tabs needs a
  coordinated tablist/tab/panel schema that its CSS record does not provide. Do not promise every
  CSS record or claim complete coverage. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components
  unless a real renderer exposes them as components.
- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary and compose Pantoken-specific
  components with it where supported.
- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary. A2UI v1.0 permits Pantoken components
  to use their own `@catalogId` alongside Basic Catalog components.
- **Docs:** add a searchable, browse-only catalog with schemas, support status, and raw JSON.
  Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.

## Architecture and safety constraints

- The version gate found a mismatch between the current SDK overview and published renderer
  bundles. Target v1.0 only. Verify v1.0 catalog and Universal registration APIs against released
  React/Lit/Angular packages before claiming support.
- If those released SDKs do not support v1.0 Universal components, stop at the adapter gate and
  choose between waiting for compatible SDK releases and building framework-specific v1.0
  adapters. Do not fall back to v0.9.
- The schema spike must identify the canonical source for typed properties, child/slot rules,
  events/functions, icons, and accessibility behavior. Do not assume CSS modifier metadata supplies
  these contracts. If substantial new metadata or renderer behavior is required, revise the coverage
  and release scope before building the catalog.
- Before bridge implementation, define a strict component and property allowlist; reject unknown
  components and props, raw HTML/markup, unsafe URLs, unrecognized icon names, and arbitrary action
  or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.
  Add negative tests for rejected inputs.
- Keep the runtime bridge browser-safe and Node-free. Do not import `@cssdoc/*`, catalog generators,
  or other build-only code into `renderers/web-components`; generation belongs in `ai/` build
  tooling.
- Give the catalog a stable, immutable, versioned `catalogId` (a `/vN/` identity, not a mutable
  `latest` URL). Treat component/prop removal, renames, required-prop changes, and incompatible
  semantics as breaking; additions that preserve old messages are additive. Tie regeneration and
  explicit version changes to the InstUI upgrade/deprecation workflow so upstream drift cannot
  silently alter the published contract.
- Update `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` if the catalog or bridge adds input surfaces or controls.

## Milestones

1. **Verification and schema/security spike.** Record the exact published package versions and the
   v1.0 Universal compatibility gap. Inspect Button, Tabs, and Tooltip; establish limited initial
   coverage and missing canonical metadata. Specify the allowlist and negative security cases.
2. **Catalog contract and generator.** Add the canonical A2UI 1.0 web catalog in `ai/` for Button
   and Tooltip, with explicit typed properties/actions/children, a stable versioned `catalogId`,
   and Basic Catalog composition via v1.0 semantics. Test schema validity, coverage, and drift.
   Publish the catalog and agent guidance with changesets for changed package output.
3. **Universal web bridge.** Implement the thin A2UI 1.0 Universal Web Component integration over
   existing Button and Tooltip elements only after the SDK gate passes. Reuse existing behavior;
   add no native UI kit and no duplicated rendering implementation. Test allowlisted props,
   children, actions, and rejected input.
4. **Docs catalog browser.** Generate static browser data from the same catalog source. Reuse the
   shadcn browser's search/static-data patterns, not its install commands or previews. Show
   per-client support, schemas, props, children, actions, raw JSON, and v1.0 web-only registration
   examples; localize new UI in English and Hungarian. Label Tabs and other unshipped components
   unsupported rather than implying full coverage.
5. **Agent evaluations, release, and drift gates.** Keep existing A2UI token-theming evaluations.
   Add positive web catalog routing and negative evaluations for invented components, invalid
   properties, and unsupported native registration. Update `use-a2ui` so agents use the Pantoken
   catalog for supported web clients and the Basic Catalog plus Pantoken tokens for native. Run
   focused tests, security checks, package checks, and publish checks. Ship each independently
   releasable package change with its changeset; follow repository release policy for docs-only
   work.

## Expected source areas

- `formats/components/src/` and `renderers/web-components/src/` — source-contract audit and web
  component behavior.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/`, and package metadata — canonical catalog,
  generation, published assets, and version/drift checks.
- `renderers/web-components/` — thin Universal Web Component bridge, with no build-only imports.
- `docs/scripts/`, `docs/a2ui/`, and `docs/.vitepress/theme/` — generated static data, browser,
  routing, localization, and focused tests.
- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/` and `packages/scaffold/assets/` — updated skill and shared
  consumer guidance.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/` and renderer tests — positive and negative agent/bridge behavior.
- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, package documentation, and `.changeset/` — security and release
  updates when applicable.

## Verification

- Verify v1.0 Universal registration and catalog composition against the exact released SDKs before
  adding any React/Lit/Angular support claim. Do not validate by using 0.9.1 packages.
- Use the Button/Tabs/Tooltip spike to validate schema-source sufficiency; test only Button and
  Tooltip in the initial catalog, and mark Tabs/other components unsupported until their contracts
  are defined.
- Validate the generated catalog against the selected A2UI schema and assert its versioned ID,
  allowlist, and drift behavior.
- Test web registration and property/child/icon/event behavior, including unsafe/unknown inputs;
  verify the browser runtime graph remains Node-free.
- Verify the docs browser uses generated catalog data, localizes its UI, and labels native support
  as schema-only without native registration examples.
- Run existing and new A2UI Waza evaluations, focused package tests, `vp check`, and applicable
  publish checks. Add changesets for package output and public behavior changes.

# Use pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines pantoken with an A2UI renderer. Pantoken supplies
design tokens and icons; A2UI supplies the UI protocol and framework-specific renderers. For
token-only work, reuse the installed A2UI renderer rather than adding a runtime, transport, renderer,
or custom catalog.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve pantoken, or
generic pantoken styling without A2UI. Use it for custom catalogs only when the user explicitly
requests one.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Identify the actual A2UI
renderer, its protocol version, and how the host framework applies themes. Check the current
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/) rather than assuming all
frameworks support the same protocol version or styling API. A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the
renderer; don't put theme properties in v1.0 protocol messages.

## 2. Apply pantoken to the existing renderer

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read
  the installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use
  pantoken's `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching,
  correctly typed token from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined.
  Keep the mapping scoped when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code color values or
  invent A2UI or InstUI property names.
- **Native clients:** Use pantoken's existing target output for the host: `pantoken generate
  flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's native theme API;
  CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- **Other web frameworks:** Choose the matching official A2UI renderer first, then use its supported
  theming mechanism. Don't assume React-specific setup applies to Lit or Angular.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; only add a custom component when
  the user asks for one.

## 3. Extend only when requested

If the user asks for a custom A2UI catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. A catalog defines agent-facing components and functions; pantoken tokens don't implement those
components or behaviors. Preserve the renderer's accessibility, focus, and interaction contracts.
Handle protocol transports only when explicitly in scope.

## 4. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference exists in the
installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI renderer version.

import { buttonCss } from "@pantoken/components";
import type { ElementDefinition } from "../lib/context.ts";

/**
 * `<instui-button>` — a token-styled `<button>`. The `variant` attribute maps to the `-color-<variant>`
 * modifier (`secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `danger`, `ai`, …); `margin` adds spacing around the
 * host (InstUI keywords like `small` / `medium large`); slotted content is the label.
 *
 * It is also a native invoker: `popovertarget` (with optional `popovertargetaction`) toggles any
 * light-DOM `[popover]` such as `<instui-context-view>`, `<instui-popover>`, or `<instui-tray>`, and
 * `command`/`commandfor` drives the command-based components (`<instui-modal>` with `--show`/`--close`,
 * etc.). The id is forwarded to the inner button via the invoker IDL, so it resolves across the shadow
 * boundary and may point forward to an element declared later in the document.
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <instui-button variant="primary" margin="small">Save changes</instui-button>
 * <instui-button variant="danger" margin="small">Delete</instui-button>
 * <instui-button popovertarget="cv">Details</instui-button>
 * <instui-context-view id="cv">More about this item.</instui-context-view>
 * ```
 */
export const button: ElementDefinition = {
  name: "button",
  define: (ctx) =>
    ctx.wrapper(
      "instui-button",
      buttonCss(ctx.I),
      (host) =>
        `<button class="${ctx.variantClass("button", host)}" part="button"><slot></slot></button>`,
      { invoker: true },
    ),
};

Contents of https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/:
# v1.0 Protocol Specification

Current Specification

**A2UI v1.0** is the current specification. Compared to [v0.9.1](/specification/v0.9.1-a2ui/), v1.0 renames the wire envelopes to `agent_to_renderer` and `renderer_to_agent`, prefixes dynamic bindings with `@` (`@path` and `@call`) and component envelope keys with `@` (`@catalogId`, `@accessibility`, `@metadata`, `@checks`), adds bidirectional function RPC messages (`callRendererFunction`, `callAgentFunction`, `rendererFunctionResponse`, `agentFunctionResponse`), and supports per-component `@catalogId` mixing and single-message `createSurface` payloads. See the [v1.0 Evolution Guide](/specification/v1.0-evolution-guide/) and [v1.0 JSON Schemas](/specification/v1.0/schemas/).

A Specification for a JSON-Based, Streaming UI Protocol.

**Version:** 1.0 · **Status:** Current · **Created:** Nov 20, 2025 · **Last Updated:** Jun 8, 2026

## Introduction

The A2UI Protocol is designed for dynamically rendering user interfaces from a stream of JSON objects sent from an agent. Its core philosophy emphasizes a clean separation of UI structure and application data, enabling progressive rendering as the renderer processes each message.

Communication occurs via a stream of JSON objects. The renderer parses each object as a distinct message and incrementally builds or updates the UI. The agent-to-renderer protocol defines four message types:

*   `createSurface`: Signals the renderer to create a new surface and begin rendering it.
*   `updateComponents`: Provides a list of component definitions to be added to or updated in a specific surface.
*   `updateDataModel`: Provides new data to be inserted into or to replace a surface's data model.
*   `deleteSurface`: Explicitly removes a surface and its contents from the UI.

End of agent turn is signaled by [transport layer](/concepts/messages/).

## Changes from previous versions

The major differences between version 1.0 and 0.9 (including 0.9.1) are:

*   **Bidirectional Function Calls**: Supports explicit, typed function invocation messages (`callRendererFunction`, `callAgentFunction`, `rendererFunctionResponse`, and `agentFunctionResponse`) verified against runtime catalog definitions.
*   **Single-Message UI Instantiation**: Allows initial component trees and data models to be embedded directly within `createSurface`, enabling complete UI composition in a single payload.
*   **Decoupled Branding**: Removes rigid theme properties (removing hardcoded brand colors) to defer visual styling entirely to the target framework's native theme. A v1.0 `createSurface` that carries `theme` is invalid.
*   **Enhanced Catalog Schemas**: Refactors function definitions into object maps for direct O(1) lookups and supports standard JSON Schema metadata fields (`$schema`, `$id`) on inline catalogs.
*   **Strict Identifier & Context Standards**: Enforces Unicode (UAX #31) naming rules across all catalog entities and reserves the `@` namespace for universal system context evaluations (such as `@index`).

See [the evolution guide](/specification/v1.0-evolution-guide/) for a detailed explanation of the differences between v0.9 and v1.0.

## Protocol overview & data flow

The A2UI protocol uses a unidirectional stream of JSON messages from the agent to the renderer to describe and update the UI. The renderer consumes this stream, builds the UI, and renders it. User interactions are handled separately, typically by sending events to a different endpoint, which may in turn trigger new messages on the UI stream.

Here is an example sequence of events (which don't have to be in exactly this order):

1.  **Create Surface:** The agent sends a `createSurface` message to initialize the surface.
2.  **Update Surface:** Once a surface has been created, the agent sends one or more `updateComponents` messages containing the definitions for all the components that will be part of the surface.
3.  **Update Data Model:** Once a surface has been created, the agent can send `updateDataModel` messages at any time to populate or change the data that the UI components will display.
4.  **Render:** The renderer renders the UI for the surface, using the component definitions to build the structure and the data model to populate the content.
5.  **Dynamic updates:** As the user interacts with the application or as new information becomes available, the agent can send additional `updateComponents` and `updateDataModel` messages to dynamically change the UI.
6.  **Delete Surface:** When a UI region is no longer needed, the agent sends a `deleteSurface` message to remove it.

```


sequenceDiagram



    participant Agent



    participant Renderer







    Agent->>+Renderer: 1. createSurface(surfaceId: "main")



    Agent->>+Renderer: 2. updateComponents(surfaceId: "main", components: [...])



    Agent->>+Renderer: 3. updateDataModel(surfaceId: "main", path: "/user", value: "Alice")



    User->>+Renderer: Interact with UI (e.g. click button)



    Renderer->>+Agent: action(name: "submit", context: {...})



    Renderer-->>-Agent: (UI is displayed)







    Note over Renderer, Agent: Time passes, user interacts, or new data arrives...







    Agent->>+Renderer: 4. updateComponents or updateDataModel (Dynamic Update)



    Note right of Renderer: Renderer re-renders the UI to reflect changes



    Renderer-->>-Agent: (UI is updated)







    Agent->>+Renderer: 5. deleteSurface(surfaceId: "main")



    Note right of Renderer: Renderer removes the UI for the "main" surface



    Renderer-->>-Agent: (UI is gone)

```

## Transport decoupling

The A2UI protocol is designed to be transport-agnostic. It defines the JSON message structure and the semantic contract between the Agent and the Renderer, but it does not mandate a specific transport layer.

### The transport contract

To support A2UI, a transport layer must fulfill the following contract:

1.  **Reliable delivery**: Messages must be delivered in the order they were generated. A2UI relies on stateful updates (e.g., creating a surface before updating it), so out-of-order delivery can corrupt the UI state.
2.  **Message framing**: The transport must clearly delimit individual JSON envelope messages (e.g., using newlines in JSONL, WebSocket frames, or SSE events).
3.  **Metadata support**: The transport must provide a mechanism to associate metadata with messages. This is critical for:
    *   **Data model synchronization**: The `sendDataModel` feature requires the renderer to send the current data model state as metadata alongside user actions.
    *   **Capabilities exchange**: Renderer capabilities (supported catalogs, custom components) and Agent capabilities are exchanged via metadata or transport-specific handshakes (like Agent Cards in A2A or initialization in MCP).
4.  **Bidirectional capability (optional)**: While the rendering stream is unidirectional (Agent -> Renderer), interactive applications require a return channel for `action` messages (Renderer -> Agent).

### Transport bindings

While A2UI is transport agnostic, it is most commonly used with the following transports.

#### AG-UI (Agent-to-User Interface) binding

**[AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction)** is the standard transport binding for Agent-to-User Interaction. It provides convenient integrations into many agent frameworks and frontends, offering low-latency and shared-state message passing between frontends and agentic backends.

#### A2A (Agent-to-Agent) binding

The **[A2A Extension](/specification/v1.0-a2ui-extension-specification/)** maps A2UI over the **[A2A Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org)**. It standardizes metadata placement, renderer-to-agent capability negotiation, and bidirectional data model synchronization for agent-to-agent interactions.

#### MCP (Model Context Protocol) binding

**[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro)** is a standard protocol for exposing data and tools to LLMs. A2UI can be carried over MCP tool calls, tool outputs, or resource subscriptions, allowing agents to dynamically render rich user interfaces for renderer-side applications.

#### Other transports

A2UI can also be carried over:

*   **[SSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Server-sent_events) with [JSON RPC](https://www.jsonrpc.org/)**: Standard server-sent events for web integrations that support streaming, and JSON RPC for renderer-agent communication.
*   **[WebSockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebSocket)**: For bidirectional, real-time sessions.
*   **[REST](https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-rest-api?hl=en)**: For simple use case, REST APIs will work but lack streaming capabilities.

## The protocol schemas

A2UI v1.0 is defined by three interacting JSON schemas.

### Common types

The [`common_types.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json) schema defines reusable primitives used throughout the protocol.

*   **`DynamicString` / `DynamicNumber` / `DynamicBoolean` / `DynamicStringList`**: The core of the data binding system. Any property that can be bound to data is defined as a `Dynamic*` type. It accepts either a literal value, a `DataBinding` (`{"@path": "..."}` using [JSON Pointer](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901)), or a `FunctionCall` (`{"@call": "...", "args": {...}}`). When a `DynamicBoolean` resolves to a `ValidationResult` object (an object with a boolean `valid` property), it is coerced to `result.valid`; strings, numbers, `null`, objects, and arrays are coerced as defined under [`DynamicBoolean` and `CheckRule` Coercion](#dynamicboolean-and-checkrule-coercion).

*   **`ChildList`**: Defines how containers hold children. It supports:

    *   `array`: A static array of `ComponentId` component references.
    *   `object`: A template for generating children from a list in the data model (requires a template `componentId` and a JSON Pointer `path` string; note that `path` here is a plain string property on the template object, not a `DataBinding` `{"@path": "..."}` object).
*   **`ComponentId`**: A reference to the unique ID of another component within the same surface.

*   **`AccessibilityAttributes`**: Standardized accessibility properties attached via `ComponentCommon.@accessibility` to any component, supporting `label` (`DynamicString`), `description` (`DynamicString`), `live` (`"off"` | `"polite"` | `"assertive"`), and `hidden` (`DynamicBoolean`).

### Agent to renderer message structure: the envelope

The [`agent_to_renderer.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json) schema is the top-level entry point. Every message streamed by the agent must validate against this schema. It handles the message dispatching.

### The Basic Catalog

The [`catalogs/basic/catalog.json`](/specification/v1.0-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#basic_catalog.json) schema contains the definitions for all specific UI components (e.g., `Text`, `Button`, `Row`) and functions (e.g., `required`, `email`).

**Swappable Catalogs & Validation:**

The [`agent_to_renderer.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json) envelope schema is designed to be catalog-agnostic. Within its `Component` definition (referenced by `ComponentsList`), it validates base properties against `common_types.json#/$defs/ComponentCommon` and references components using a placeholder filename: `catalog.json` (specifically `$ref: "catalog.json#/$defs/anyComponent"`).

To validate A2UI messages:

1.  **Basic Catalog**: Map `catalog.json` to `catalogs/basic/catalog.json`.
2.  **Renderer Catalog**: Map `catalog.json` to your own catalog file (e.g., `my_company_catalog.json`).

This indirection allows the same core envelope schema to be used with any compliant component catalog without modification.

Defining your own catalog allows you to restrict the agent to using exactly the components and visual language that exist in your application. To use your own catalog, simply include it in the prompt in place of the basic catalog. It shou

---
name: use-a2ui
description: Inspect an app's installed A2UI renderer and apply pantoken tokens or icons through its supported theme API. Use for A2UI renderer theming or native token output, not transport-only or generic pantoken tasks.
---

# Use pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines pantoken with an A2UI renderer. Pantoken supplies
design tokens and icons; A2UI supplies the UI protocol and framework-specific renderers. For
token-only work, reuse the installed A2UI renderer rather than adding a runtime, transport, renderer,
or custom catalog.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve pantoken, or
generic pantoken styling without A2UI. Use it for custom catalogs only when the user explicitly
requests one.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Identify the actual A2UI
renderer, its protocol version, and how the host framework applies themes. Check the current
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/) rather than assuming all
frameworks support the same protocol version or styling API. A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the
renderer; don't put theme properties in v1.0 protocol messages.

## 2. Apply pantoken to the existing renderer

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read
  the installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use
  pantoken's `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching,
  correctly typed token from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined.
  Keep the mapping scoped when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code color values or
  invent A2UI or InstUI property names.
- **Native clients:** Use pantoken's existing target output for the host: `pantoken generate
  flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's native theme API;
  CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- **Other web frameworks:** Choose the matching official A2UI renderer first, then use its supported
  theming mechanism. Don't assume React-specific setup applies to Lit or Angular.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; only add a custom component when
  the user asks for one.

## 3. Extend only when requested

If the user asks for a custom A2UI catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. A catalog defines agent-facing components and functions; pantoken tokens don't implement those
components or behaviors. Preserve the renderer's accessibility, focus, and interaction contracts.
Handle protocol transports only when explicitly in scope.

## 4. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference exists in the
installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI renderer version.

## References

- [A2UI v1.0 protocol](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)
- [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)
- [A2UI client integration](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/)
- [A2UI catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/)

import { buttonCss } from "@pantoken/components";
import type { ElementDefinition } from "../lib/context.ts";

/**
 * `<instui-button>` — a token-styled `<button>`. The `variant` attribute maps to the `-color-<variant>`
 * modifier (`secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `danger`, `ai`, …); `margin` adds spacing around the
 * host (InstUI keywords like `small` / `medium large`); slotted content is the label.
 *
 * It is also a native invoker: `popovertarget` (with optional `popovertargetaction`) toggles any
 * light-DOM `[popover]` such as `<instui-context-view>`, `<instui-popover>`, or `<instui-tray>`, and
 * `command`/`commandfor` drives the command-based components (`<instui-modal>` with `--show`/`--close`,
 * etc.). The id is forwarded to the inner button via the invoker IDL, so it resolves across the shadow
 * boundary and may point forward to an element declared later in the document.
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <instui-button variant="primary" margin="small">Save changes</instui-button>
 * <instui-button variant="danger" margin="small">Delete</instui-button>
 * <instui-button popovertarget="cv">Details</instui-button>
 * <instui-context-view id="cv">More about this item.</instui-context-view>
 * ```
 */
export const button: ElementDefinition = {
  name: "button",
  define: (ctx) =>
    ctx.wrapper(
      "instui-button",
      buttonCss(ctx.I),
      (host) =>
        `<button class="${ctx.variantClass("button", host)}" part="button"><slot></slot></button>`,
      { invoker: true },
    ),
};

# Security policy

## Supported versions

pantoken publishes many small packages from this monorepo, all versioned together. We support the
latest published release of each package. Fixes land on `main` and ship in the next release; we don't
backport to older lines.

## Security requirements and scope

pantoken is a design-token transformation and distribution system. It converts Instructure design tokens and icons into CSS, framework integrations, build-tool plugins, design-tool data, and generated platform source. It is not an authentication, authorization, cryptography, or application-security library.

### What users can expect

- Published downstream packages use a vendored, versioned token model and do not require consumers to retrieve the GitHub-hosted upstream design-token source.
- Generated output is reproducible from the repository source and pinned dependencies.
- Tokens Studio colour modifiers from the pinned upstream source are validated for structure,
  operation, colour space, numeric range, reference integrity, and colour type before publication.
  Malformed modifiers are recorded for review and block replacement of generated artifacts until an
  explicit rewrite is supplied.
- npm releases include provenance linking the package to its source commit and GitHub Actions workflow.
- The project tests token resolution, output generation, reference integrity, package exports, and supported integrations in continuous integration.
- Reported vulnerabilities affecting the latest release will be investigated and, when confirmed, fixed in a subsequent release.

### Security boundaries and limitations

- Component accessibility audits execute trusted repository examples and locally built browser
  bundles through automatica11y and Chrome/Chromium. They aren't a sandbox for untrusted fixtures
  or a sanitizer. Reports may contain example markup and simulated screen-reader output; don't put
  secrets in examples. Automated accessibility findings aren't a security or WCAG attestation.
  API documentation publishes an explicitly imported, reviewed summary from local reports.
  The importer validates inventories and counts and escapes report-derived Markdown text; it isn't
  an untrusted-report upload service. Snapshots can lag source changes and aren't build attestations.

- Token values, plugin implementations, configuration files, Markdown, HTML, and other caller-provided content must be treated as trusted input unless the relevant package explicitly documents otherwise.
- pantoken emitters transform input into CSS, JavaScript, JSON, markup, or platform source. They are not a general-purpose sanitizer for untrusted input. Passing attacker-controlled values to an emitter or plugin may produce unsafe output, including CSS, markup, or code injection.
- Generated stylesheets, components, and framework integrations do not provide an application security boundary. Applications remain responsible for authentication, authorization, output encoding, Content Security Policy, browser security, and safe handling of user content.
- Application-controlled Pendo guide classes, compact color/glyph suffixes, and layout attributes select stylesheet presentation rules. They do not validate or sanitize Pendo-injected guide HTML, which remains trusted consumer content.
- Browser component configuration, including numeric attributes and CSS custom properties such as ProgressBar's `min`/`value-now`/`value-max`, Alert's `--timeout`, and ProgressCircle's `--animation-delay`, is application-controlled. Web components and interaction helpers that consume numeric configuration validate expected ranges, but input-type hints such as `initInPlaceEdit`'s do not validate committed values. Applications remain responsible for validating those values and deciding which elements may be updated, dismissed, or animated. The Canvas theme editor accepts only positive safe integers for custom preview widths.
- SkeletonLoader's parent loading-region helper accepts application-supplied state events and announcement labels. It writes labels as text, not HTML, and requires initially empty status and error elements outside the busy region in the application's server-rendered markup. It does not sanitize application content or control which results the application renders.
- DrawerLayout's `tray-label` and `content-label` values become `aria-label` attribute strings on
  its shadow regions, not parsed HTML. Applications must supply descriptive, nonempty names.
- FormField's opt-in native-validation helper checks browser constraint validity and associates an
  authored error by ID. It requires the control and a separate, named error with message text inside
  the host, preserves hint references, and doesn't parse messages as HTML. Applications own the
  rules, message content, and server-side validation; client-side validity isn't an authorization
  or input-sanitization boundary.
- Menu navigation is opt-in and accepts a connected native popover and its button in the same root.
  It excludes nested-menu events and blocks ARIA-disabled activation in a menu capture listener.
  Those presentation controls aren't authorization: applications own action effects, checked state,
  and permission checks. Menu IDs and trigger relationships must remain stable.
- TreeBrowser's application-supplied `aria-owns` references must identify groups inside the same
  tree that don't contain the owning row. The behavior rejects missing, external, and non-group
  references and excludes nested-tree events. This scopes DOM updates; it doesn't sanitize markup
  or validate every ARIA relationship.
  Applications must provide unique IDs and reinitialize the manual behavior after replacing markup.
- pantoken plugins execute with the privileges of the Node.js build or application process that loads them. Plugin structure is validated by `validatePlugin` (non-empty name, function hooks, no unrecognised keys) and plugin output is validated at the IR boundary before it enters the token graph. Full execution sandboxing is planned. Only trusted plugins and configuration should be used.
- The CLI validates `--theme`, `--class`, and `--format` inputs against allowlists at parse time; unknown flags are rejected immediately. The CLI warns when the output path escapes the current working directory but still writes to the caller-selected location.
- `@pantoken/plugin-custom-theme-colors` accepts an arbitrary brand color for its `custom` scale (as the Canvas theme editor's Custom swatch does). Only `#rgb`/`#rrggbb` is accepted, and anything else throws a `TypeError`. The generated CSS contains only derived `#rrggbb` values, never the raw input string. Posted `customScale`/`customColor` values in demo and editor frames are dropped unless every entry is a plain hex.
- Repository translation sources are trusted input. Entries marked `verbatim: "required"` bypass external translation adapters and are copied exactly into locale caches; `allow` only permits a model response to match the source.
- Generated documentation binds current machine values into stable translation templates. Missing,
  duplicated, unknown, or malformed slots fail validation; the bindings don't evaluate expressions
  or follow object paths. Source Markdown and URLs remain trusted inputs, not sanitized content.
  Migration preserves fuzzy status and rejects ambiguous mappings rather than approving translations.
- The CLI translation HTTP shim can listen only on `127.0.0.1`. It rejects browser `Origin`
  headers and unexpected `Host` headers before invoking a provider. It is an unencrypted local
  development endpoint, not a remote service or an authentication boundary against local processes.
- Scope and docs theme broadcasts use concrete iframe origins. Wildcard delivery is limited to
  explicitly sandboxed `srcdoc` previews without `allow-same-origin`; malformed and other opaque
  frame URLs are skipped. These messages carry public presentation settings, never credentials or
  confidential application state.
- `@pantoken/tinymce-save` persists trusted author snapshots in origin-local localStorage. Presets
  may contain HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and host application state; they are schema-validated before
  restoration but are not sanitized. localStorage is not secret or synchronized storage, and other
  scripts on the same origin can read or alter it. Blocked storage and quota failures leave the
  working document unchanged. Import/export actions read and write portable JSON files only through
  a browser-initiated user selection flow; they do not contact the network. Opening a preset
  containing custom JavaScript intentionally executes that code in the host editor's existing
  preview context.
- The Canvas editor's Inline provider snapshots trusted author HTML and CSS in a temporary
  script-disabled iframe. Packaged data-image glyphs are rasterized to bounded PNG canvases; author
  images and CSS resources may still need network access. Portable Inline is light-only, suppresses
  generated and custom preview JavaScript, and strips scripts/event attributes from its snapshot.
  This is not a general sanitizer or a guarantee that Canvas preserves every CSS property or data
  image. Other providers' Include interactions switch suppresses generated Pantoken scripts only;
  custom JavaScript and native browser behavior remain author-controlled.
- The public shadcn registry is an HTTPS distribution channel for package dependencies, CSS
  configuration, and usage metadata. Registry schema validation checks structure, not code quality
  or project suitability. Inspect an item with `shadcn view`, review the resulting diff, and pin
  package versions for durable applications. npm provenance covers installed packages but does not
  sign the mutable JSON served from `pantoken.app`.
- Agent coding sessions are checkpointed by Entire and pushed to this repository as git objects
  under `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`. Transcripts are redacted at capture time for known credential
  formats and for email and phone PII, but they are still a record of contributor terminal and
  editor activity. Do not paste live credentials into an agent session; use environment variables
  and short-lived tokens instead. Redaction configuration lives in `.entire/settings.json`.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report security issues privately. Don't open a public issue for anything security-sensitive.

- Use GitHub's [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/security/advisories/new)
  to open a draft advisory. This is the preferred channel.
- If you can't use GitHub, email <[REDACTED_EMAIL]>.

Please include enough detail to reproduce the issue: affected package and version, a description of the
impact, and steps or a proof of concept. We'll acknowledge your report within five business days and
keep you updated as we work on a fix.

## Vulnerability response process

When a vulnerability is reported, the project will:

1. Acknowledge the report within five business days.
2. Privately assess and attempt to reproduce the issue, identify affected packages and versions, and evaluate its severity and impact.
3. Coordinate with the reporter through the private advisory or email channel and request any additional information needed.
4. Develop a fix privately, including regression tests where practical, and check related packages for the same weakness.
5. Release the fix for the latest supported version and document the security-relevant change in the affected package changelog.
6. Publish a GitHub security advisory after the fix is available, including affected versions, impact, remediation, and upgrade instructions.
7. Credit the reporter unless they request anonymity.

- [`vite.config.ts`](vite.config.ts): test discovery, V8 coverage, enforced thresholds, property-test
  setup, and the development gate.
- [`codecov.yml`](codecov.yml): project and patch coverage reporting.
- [`tools/validate-generated/index.ts`](tools/validate-generated/index.ts): generated-file,
  reference-integrity, CLI-target, and published-CSS checks.
- [`scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts`](scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts):
  package metadata, provenance configuration, engine, license, and export prerequisites.
- [Release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml): scoped release permissions, build and package
  gates, OIDC publishing, and immutable GitHub releases.
- [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md): supported versions, security requirements, reporting and response,
  supply-chain controls, and release-verification instructions.

## Residual risks and limitations

The following risks remain or are deliberately outside the security claim:

- **Generated-value localization.** Placeholder validation checks binding integrity, not translation
  quality or source safety. Bindings contain trusted repository Markdown and URLs; substitution
  doesn't sanitize them. Migration can't approve fuzzy translations or infer ambiguous repeated
  values. Those entries require review before cache-only rendering can publish updated values.
  The control rejects missing, duplicated, unknown, and malformed slots without evaluating code;
  evidence is in `tools/translation-adapters/tests/generated-values.test.ts` and
  `scripts/release/migrate-generated-values.test.ts`.

- **Accessibility fixture execution.** Audit examples and their production behavior scripts execute
  in Chrome/Chromium with local-process privileges. They are trusted repository code, not isolated
  untrusted content. Audit reports may contain authored markup. Accessibility findings, conditions
  checks, and simulated screen-reader output don't prove security or WCAG conformance.
  Published API evidence is a historical, contributor-reviewed snapshot. Report files are trusted
  local inputs, not an upload endpoint or a sandbox; imported counts don't attest to the current
  source revision. Don't put confidential material in fixtures, report metadata, or findings.

- **Tree ownership metadata.** TreeBrowser markup and IDs are application-controlled. Group
  containment checks limit behavior updates to the tree; they don't sanitize markup or make
  untrusted tree content safe. Applications must keep IDs unique and reinitialize the manual
  behavior after replacing tree markup.

- **Drawer landmark names.** Applications supply nonempty tray and content labels. DrawerLayout
  writes labels through `setAttribute`, not HTML parsing; tests cover literal markup-like text.
  This prevents label text from creating elements, but doesn't sanitize slotted content.

- **Native form validation.** Browser constraints and `setCustomValidity()` are application-owned.
  Opt-in FormField behavior manages presentation and ARIA associations, not server validation,
  authorization, or sanitization. Error IDs must stay unique; reinitialize after changing IDs or
  moving a control to another form. Real assistive-technology review remains necessary.

- **Menu actions.** Menu navigation handles focus and presentation, not action authorization.
  Applications own click effects and checked state, must use stable IDs and correct roles, and must
  authorize actions independently. Submenus and menubars aren't implemented by this helper.

- **Automated maintenance evidence.** Compatibility tests do not establish visual equivalence,

Inline conversion does not change this trust boundary. Its temporary snapshot frame disables
    scripts, but referenced author resources may still access the network; the generic interactions
    toggle in other providers is not a sandbox for custom scripts or authored active content.
11. **Agent transcript scanning.** Entire's checkpoint transcripts are dense with structural UUIDs,
    which GitHub's legacy npm-token detector matches whenever the keyword `npm` appears nearby. In
    an npm monorepo that fires constantly and blocks the checkpoint push, so
    `.github/secret_scanning.yml` excludes `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl`, and `prompt.txt` from
    GitHub secret scanning. Redaction at capture time (T-17) is therefore the primary control for
    credentials in transcripts, and GitHub scanning no longer backstops it on those paths. The
    exclusion is scoped to file names the repository does not otherwise track, and takes effect only
    once present on the default branch.
12. **Platform release monitoring.** External feeds can be stale, unavailable, or incorrectly mapped
    to an adapter; packages without a trustworthy version feed still need manual review. A scheduled
    issue is a prompt to test a release, not a compatibility attestation or automatic package update.

13. **Local translation transport.** The HTTP shim is restricted to IPv4 loopback and rejects
    browser-origin and unexpected-host requests. It does not provide TLS or authenticate other
    local processes; it must not be exposed through a proxy or used as a remote translation service.
14. **Opaque preview origins.** Sandboxed `srcdoc` frames without `allow-same-origin` require wildcard
    target origins. Scope and docs broadcasts restrict that exception to those frames and carry
    only public presentation settings. Callers must never use these channels for secrets or
    confidential application state.

These limitations do not weaken the narrower requirements in SR-1 through SR-6 because they are
included in the documented scope and trust model. They do prevent Pantoken from claiming that it
safely accepts arbitrary untrusted transformation input.

## Maintenance of this assurance case

The maintainer should review this document:

- When a new public input surface, plugin type, network operation, or privileged workflow is added.
- When the trust model or security requirements in `SECURITY.md` change.
- After a confirmed vulnerability reveals a missing threat or ineffective control.
- When release, signing, dependency, or CI infrastructure changes materially.
- At least annually as part of the roadmap and security-documentation review.

name: use-a2ui
description: Inspect an app's installed A2UI renderer and apply pantoken tokens or icons through its supported theme API. Use for A2UI renderer theming or native token output, not transport-only or generic pantoken tasks.
---

# Use pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines pantoken with an A2UI renderer. Pantoken supplies
design tokens and icons; A2UI supplies the UI protocol and framework-specific renderers. For
token-only work, reuse the installed A2UI renderer rather than adding a runtime, transport, renderer,
or custom catalog.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve pantoken, or
generic pantoken styling without A2UI. Use it for custom catalogs only when the user explicitly
requests one.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Identify the actual A2UI
renderer, its protocol version, and how the host framework applies themes. Check the current
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/) rather than assuming all
frameworks support the same protocol version or styling API. A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the
renderer; don't put theme properties in v1.0 protocol messages.

## 2. Apply pantoken to the existing renderer

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read
  the installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use
  pantoken's `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching,
  correctly typed token from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined.
  Keep the mapping scoped when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code color values or
  invent A2UI or InstUI property names.
- **Native clients:** Use pantoken's existing target output for the host: `pantoken generate
  flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's native theme API;
  CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- **Other web frameworks:** Choose the matching official A2UI renderer first, then use its supported
  theming mechanism. Don't assume React-specific setup applies to Lit or Angular.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; only add a custom component when
  the user asks for one.

## 3. Extend only when requested

If the user asks for a custom A2UI catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. A catalog defines agent-facing components and functions; pantoken tokens don't implement those
components or behaviors. Preserve the renderer's accessibility, focus, and interaction contracts.
Handle protocol transports only when explicitly in scope.

## 4. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference exists in the
installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI renderer version.

## References

- [A2UI v1.0 protocol](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)
- [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)
- [A2UI client integration](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/)
- [A2UI catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/)

*** Begin Patch
*** Delete File: /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/SKILL.md
*** Add File: /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/SKILL.md
+---
+name: use-a2ui
+description: Use Pantoken's constrained A2UI 1.0 component catalog or theme an installed A2UI renderer with Pantoken tokens. Use for A2UI work involving Pantoken, not transport-only or generic Pantoken tasks.
+---
+
+# Use Pantoken with A2UI
+
+Use this skill when a consumer app combines Pantoken with A2UI. A2UI supplies the protocol and
+framework-specific renderers; Pantoken supplies tokens, icons, and a small set of styled components.
+Use A2UI 1.0 only. Do not fall back to A2UI 0.9.
+
+## Do not use this skill for
+
+Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve Pantoken, or for
+generic Pantoken styling without A2UI.
+
+## 1. Identify the client and versions
+
+Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Confirm the A2UI protocol
+version and the client framework's supported SDK version from the
+[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
+[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/). A2UI 1.0 delegates branding
+to the renderer; don't put theme properties in protocol messages.
+
+## 2. Prefer the Pantoken catalog for verified Lit clients
+
+For A2UI 1.0 Lit clients, use the published Pantoken catalog and Universal components:
+
+- Install `@pantoken/ai` and `@pantoken/web-components`.
+- Register `pantokenA2uiCatalog` with `registerPantokenA2uiComponents()` from
+  `@pantoken/web-components/a2ui`, alongside A2UI's Basic Catalog.
+- Reference Pantoken components with the catalog's `@catalogId`.
+- Use only the components and properties listed in the catalog JSON at
+  `@pantoken/ai/a2ui/catalog-v1.json` or the
+  [Pantoken A2UI Catalog](https://pantoken.app/a2ui/). The v1 catalog currently contains
+  `PantokenButton` and `PantokenTooltip`; don't invent additional Pantoken components or properties.
+- The catalog defines no executable functions. Its actions dispatch through A2UI's normal
+  action-handling path; the host application remains responsible for authorization.
+
+React and Angular v1.0 runtime support has not been verified. For those clients, use A2UI's Basic
+Catalog and the installed renderer's theme API instead of claiming the Pantoken Universal components
+are supported. Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose have schema-only support; Pantoken does not
+provide native component renderers.
+
+## 3. Theme the Basic Catalog and other verified renderers
+
+- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read the
+  installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use Pantoken's
+  `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching, correctly typed token
+  from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined. Keep mappings scoped
+  when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code colors or invent property names.
+- **Native clients:** Use Pantoken's existing target output for the host:
+  `pantoken generate flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's
+  native theme API; CSS custom properties don't apply to native views.
+- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
+  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; don't invent icon props.
+
+## 4. Extend only when requested
+
+If the user explicitly requests a different custom catalog, follow A2UI's
+[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
+API. Preserve strict property allowlists, avoid raw HTML and URL-bearing props, and don't add
+executable catalog functions without an explicit design and security review. A catalog schema is
+not an authorization boundary; the host must authorize action effects.
+
+## 5. Verify
+
+Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
+including contrast, keyboard behavior, and focus visibility. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference
+exists in the installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI
+renderer version.
+
